sentences.zh: ◎二高伊朱二劉範二王孟趙李任張高崇文，字崇文。

translations.literal: Two Gao, Yi, Zhu, two Liu, Fan, two Wang, Meng, Zhao, Li, Ren, and Zhang: Gao Chongwen was styled Chongwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the biographies of the two Gao, Yi, Zhu, the two Liu, Fan, the two Wang, Meng, Zhao, Li, Ren, and Zhang, Gao Chongwen bore the style name Chongwen.

sentences.zh: 其先自渤海徙幽州，七世不異居，開元中，再表其閭。

translations.literal: His ancestors moved from Bohai to Youzhou; for seven generations they did not live apart, and in the Kaiyuan era their lane was twice commended.
translations.idiomatic: His family had come from Bohai to Youzhou; seven generations lived under one roof, and in the Kaiyuan period the emperor twice honored their household.

sentences.zh: 崇文性樸重寡言，少籍平盧軍。

translations.literal: Chongwen was plain, grave, and sparing of speech; in youth he was enrolled in the Pinglu army.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwen was unassuming and taciturn; as a young man he served in the Pinglu army.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，從韓全義鎮長武城，治軍有聲。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era he followed Han Quanyi in garrisoning Changwu Fort and won a reputation for governing troops.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyuan he served under Han Quanyi at Changwu Fort and became known for discipline in camp.

sentences.zh: 累官金吾將軍。

translations.literal: He rose through posts to General of the Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step until he became a general of the Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃三萬寇寧州，崇文率兵三千往救，戰佛堂原，大破之，封渤海郡王。

translations.literal: When thirty thousand Tibetans raided Ningzhou, Chongwen led three thousand men to the relief, fought at Fotang Plain, routed them utterly, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand Tibetans attacked Ningzhou; Chongwen marched three thousand men to save the city, defeated them at Fotang Plain, and was made Prince of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 全義入朝，留知行營節度後務，遷長武城都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: When Quanyi went to court, Chongwen was left to manage the rear affairs of the expeditionary command; he was moved up to commander of all forces at Changwu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: After Quanyi departed for the capital, Chongwen remained to run the expedition's rear affairs and was appointed commander of the garrison at Changwu Fort.

sentences.zh: 劉辟反，宰相杜黃裳薦其才，詔檢校工部尚書、左神策行營節度使，俾統左右神策、麟遊奉天諸屯兵討辟。

translations.literal: When Liu Pi rebelled, the chief minister Du Huangshang recommended his talent; an edict named him acting Minister of Works and commissioner of the Left Divine Strategy expedition, charging him to command the Left and Right Divine Strategy forces and the garrisons at Linyou and Fengtian to suppress Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi rose in rebellion; Du Huangshang praised Chongwen's ability, and the throne appointed him acting Minister of Works and expeditionary commissioner of the Left Divine Strategy Army, with orders to take the Left and Right Divine Strategy troops and the Linyou and Fengtian garrisons against Pi.

sentences.zh: 時顯功宿將，人人自謂當選，及詔出，皆大驚。

translations.literal: At the time famous generals of long service each thought himself certain to be chosen; when the edict appeared, all were greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Seasoned commanders with glittering records had each assumed the post would be his; when the appointment was announced, the army was stunned.

sentences.zh: 始，崇文選兵五千，常若寇至。

translations.literal: From the first, Chongwen had chosen five thousand soldiers and kept them always as if the enemy were at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Long before this campaign Chongwen had kept five thousand picked men trained as though battle were imminent every day.

sentences.zh: 至是，卯漏受命，辰已出師，器良械完，無一不具。

translations.literal: On this occasion he received his orders at the fifth watch and marched before noon; weapons were excellent, gear complete — nothing was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: He received his orders at dawn and was on the road before midday; arms were sound, equipment full — nothing had been left undone.

sentences.zh: 過興元，士有折逆旅匕箸者，即斬以徇。

translations.literal: Passing through Xingyuan, a soldier who broke the chopsticks at an inn was immediately beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingyuan a man snapped the chopsticks at a roadside inn; Chongwen had him executed on the spot to terrify the ranks.

sentences.zh: 乃西自閬中出，卻劍門兵，解梓潼之圍，賊將邢泚退守梓州。

translations.literal: He then marched west from Langzhong, drove back the troops at Jianmen, lifted the siege of Zitong, and the rebel general Xing Ci withdrew to defend Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Swinging west from Langzhong he repulsed the force at Jianmen, relieved Zitong, and drove the rebel Xing Ci back to Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 詔拜崇文東川節度使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Chongwen military governor of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The court made him military governor of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 初，辟陷東川，執節度使李康不殺也；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Pi had seized Dongchuan he had seized the governor Li Kang but did not kill him;
translations.idiomatic: When Pi first overran Dongchuan he had taken Li Kang prisoner yet spared his life;

sentences.zh: 至是，歸康以丐雪，崇文數康失守罪，斬之。

translations.literal: now Kang was returned begging to clear his name; Chongwen recounted Kang's crime of losing his post and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was sent back pleading innocence; Chongwen listed his failures as governor and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 鹿頭山南距成都百五十里，扼二川之要，辟城之，旁連八屯，以拒東兵。

translations.literal: Lutou Mountain stood a hundred and fifty li south of Chengdu and commanded the vital ground between the two rivers; Pi walled it and linked eight camps beside it to block the eastern army.
translations.idiomatic: Lutou Mountain, a hundred and fifty li south of Chengdu, held the choke point of the two river valleys; Pi fortified it and ringed it with eight camps to stop the eastern advance.

sentences.zh: 崇文始破賊二萬於城下，會雨，不克攻。

translations.literal: Chongwen first broke twenty thousand rebels below the wall, but rain came and he could not press the assault.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwen first shattered twenty thousand rebels under the walls, yet rain fell and the attack could not be finished.

sentences.zh: 明日，戰萬勝堆，堆直鹿頭左，使驍將高霞寓鼓之，士扳緣上，矢石如雨，募死士奪而有之，盡殺戍者，焚其柵，下瞰鹿頭城，人可頭數。

translations.literal: The next day he fought at Wansheng Mound; the mound stood directly left of Lutou. He had the fierce general Gao Xiayu beat the drums; soldiers climbed hand over hand while arrows and stones fell like rain; he recruited daredevils who seized it, killed every defender, burned the palisade, and looked down on Lutou city — the men could be counted by head.
translations.idiomatic: On the morrow he fought at Wansheng Mound, which lay just west of Lutou. Gao Xiayu drummed the charge; men scaled the slope through a storm of missiles until picked warriors took the height, slaughtered the garrison, burned the stockade, and from above could count the heads in Lutou town.

sentences.zh: 凡八戰皆捷，賊心始搖。

translations.literal: In eight battles he was victorious every time, and the rebels' hearts began to waver.
translations.idiomatic: Eight engagements, eight victories — the rebels' morale began to crack.

sentences.zh: 大將阿跌光顏與崇文約，後期，懼罪，請深入自贖，乃軍鹿頭西，斷賊糧道。

translations.literal: The great general Adie Guangyan had agreed on a rendezvous with Chongwen but was late and, fearing punishment, asked to redeem himself by a deep strike; he encamped west of Lutou and cut the rebels' grain route.
translations.idiomatic: General Adie Guangyan, having missed the rendezvous and fearing blame, volunteered a daring raid; he camped west of Lutou and severed the enemy supply lines.

sentences.zh: 賊大震，其將李文悅以兵三千自歸，仇良輔舉鹿頭城二萬眾降，執辟子方叔、婿蘇強。

translations.literal: The rebels were greatly shaken; their general Li Wenyue came over with three thousand men, Qiu Liangfu surrendered Lutou with twenty thousand, and Pi's son Fangshu and son-in-law Su Qiang were seized.
translations.idiomatic: Panic swept the rebel host: Li Wenyue defected with three thousand men, Qiu Liangfu yielded Lutou and twenty thousand troops, and Pi's son Fangshu and son-in-law Su Qiang were captured.

sentences.zh: 遂趣成都，餘兵皆面縛送款。

translations.literal: He then pressed on Chengdu; the remaining troops all came forward bound to offer submission.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Chengdu; the rest of the enemy came in bonds to surrender.

sentences.zh: 辟走，追禽之，檻送京師。

translations.literal: Pi fled; he was pursued and captured and sent to the capital in a cage.
translations.idiomatic: Pi ran but was overtaken, caged, and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 入成都也，師屯大達，市井不移，珍貨如山，無秋毫之犯。

translations.literal: On entering Chengdu the army camped along the great roads; markets were undisturbed, treasures piled like hills — not a hair's breadth was taken.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered Chengdu his men encamped on the main streets; shops stayed open, riches lay in heaps, yet not the smallest thing was stolen.

sentences.zh: 邢泚已降而貳，斬於軍，衣冠脅汙者詣牙請命，崇文為條上全活之。

translations.literal: Xing Ci had already surrendered but wavered again and was executed in camp; gentry who had been forced to serve came to the headquarters to beg for their lives, and Chongwen drew up lists and memorialized to spare them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Ci, having submitted, rebelled again and was beheaded in camp; intimidated officials pleaded at headquarters, and Chongwen petitioned item by item to spare them.

sentences.zh: 進檢校司空、西川節度副大使，南平郡王，實封三百戶，刻石紀功於鹿頭山。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting Grand Master of Works and vice commissioner of the Xichuan command, enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping with a substantive fief of three hundred households, and his merit was carved in stone on Lutou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Grand Master of Works and deputy military governor of Xichuan, created Prince of Nanping with three hundred taxable households, and his victory was inscribed on Lutou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 崇文不通書，厭案牘諮判以為繁，且蜀優富無所事，請扞邊自力，乃詔同中書門下平章事、邠寧慶節度使，為京西諸軍都統。

translations.literal: Chongwen did not know letters and disliked the tangle of documents and staff judgments; moreover Shu was rich and easy and he had nothing to do, so he asked to guard the frontier by his own effort. Thereupon he was ordered Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and military governor of Bin-Ning-Qing, and made overall commander of the western capital armies.
translations.idiomatic: Illiterate and weary of paperwork, finding Shu too soft a billet, he asked for hard service on the border. The court named him Grand Councillor and governor of Bin, Ning, and Qing, and chief of the western capital armies.

sentences.zh: 崇文恃功而侈，舉蜀帑藏百工之巧者皆自隨，又不曉朝廷儀，憚於覲謁，有詔聽便道之屯。

translations.literal: Chongwen relied on his merit and lived lavishly, taking with him every skilled artisan from Shu's treasuries; he also did not understand court ceremony and shrank from audience, so an edict allowed him to go straight to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Flush with victory he lived in splendor, hauling away Shu's finest craftsmen; ignorant of court ritual and afraid to appear before the throne, he was permitted to travel directly to his command.

sentences.zh: 居邠三年，戎備整修。

translations.literal: He dwelt at Bin three years, and frontier defenses were put in good order.
translations.idiomatic: For three years at Bin he kept the frontier in excellent trim.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十四，贈司徒，謚曰威武。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-four; posthumously he was made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Majestic Martial.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-four, was posthumously made Grand Tutor, and honored as Majestic Martial.

sentences.zh: 會昌六年，詔配享憲宗廟。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Huichang an edict ordered him enshrined in the temple of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang 6 he was ordered to share sacrifice in Emperor Xianzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 子承簡，少事忠武軍，後更隸神策。

translations.literal: His son Chengjian in youth served the Zhongwu army and later was transferred to the Divine Strategy corps.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengjian first served in the Zhongwu army, then in the Divine Strategy guard.

sentences.zh: 以崇文平蜀功，除嘉王傅。

translations.literal: Because of Chongwen's merit in pacifying Shu, Chengjian was made tutor to the Prince of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: For Chongwen's conquest of Shu, Chengjian was appointed tutor to the Prince of Jia.

sentences.zh: 裴度征蔡，奏署牙將。

translations.literal: When Pei Du campaigned against Cai, he was memorialized as a headquarters guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du marched against Cai, Chengjian was named a guard officer on his staff.

sentences.zh: 蔡平，詔析上蔡、郾城、遂平、西平四縣為洲殷州，拜承簡刺史，治郾城。

translations.literal: When Cai was pacified, an edict carved out the four counties of Shangcai, Yancheng, Suiping, and Xiping to form Yin Prefecture; Chengjian was made its governor and administered Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Cai fell, the court formed Yin Prefecture from Shangcai, Yancheng, Suiping, and Xiping, and made Chengjian its governor, with his seat at Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 始開屯田，列防庸，瀕溵綿地二百里無復水敗，皆為腴田。

translations.literal: He first opened military colonies and posted defenses along the Yong; for two hundred li along the Yin the land no longer suffered flood ruin and all became rich fields.
translations.idiomatic: He opened colony fields and frontier posts; for two hundred li along the Yin floods ceased to waste the land, and the soil turned fertile.

sentences.zh: 先是，賊築武宮以誇戰勞，承簡夷其丘，庀家財以葬。

translations.literal: Earlier the rebels had built a martial shrine to boast of their victories; Chengjian leveled the mound and spent his household wealth on burials.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had raised a victory mound; Chengjian razed it and used his private fortune to bury the dead.

sentences.zh: 葺儒宮，備俎豆，歲時行禮。

translations.literal: He restored the Confucian temple, prepared the sacrificial vessels, and performed the seasonal rites each year.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the school temple, furnished the ritual vessels, and observed the seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 野有荍實，民得以食。

translations.literal: In the wilds there were buckwheat seeds, and the people were able to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Wild buckwheat grew, and the people had food.

sentences.zh: 將吏立石頌功。

translations.literal: Officers and clerks set up a stone to praise his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: His officers erected a stone praising his work.

sentences.zh: 遷邢州刺史，觀察府責賦尤急，承簡代下戶數百輸租。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Xingzhou; the observation office pressed for taxes with especial harshness, and Chengjian paid the levies for several hundred poor households.
translations.idiomatic: Made governor of Xingzhou, he found the circuit office crushing the people with taxes and paid the quotas for hundreds of poor households himself.

sentences.zh: 遷宋州。

translations.literal: He was moved to Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 會宣武將李反，遣使責財於宋，承簡囚之，前後數輩輒繫獄，一日並出斬於牙門，威震部中。

translations.literal: When a Xuanwu general surnamed Li rebelled, he sent envoys to demand wealth from Song; Chengjian imprisoned them, and several successive parties were likewise jailed; one day he had them all beheaded at headquarters, and awe filled the command.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel general of Xuanwu named Li sent men to extort money from Song; Chengjian seized every envoy, jailed batch after batch, then one morning executed them all before headquarters — and the circuit trembled.

sentences.zh: 悉兵攻之。

translations.literal: Li marched his whole force to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Li brought his entire army against him.

sentences.zh: 宋有三城，南城陷，承簡保北兩城，數與賊確。

translations.literal: Song had three walled towns; the southern city fell, and Chengjian held the two northern cities, clashing with the rebels again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Song had three citadels; the south fell, but Chengjian held the north pair and fought the rebels repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 會徐州救至，為李質所執，兵遂潰。

translations.literal: When Xuzhou relief arrived it was seized by Li Zhi, and the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Relief from Xuzhou came, but Li Zhi captured it and Chengjian's force broke.

sentences.zh: 拜兗海沂密節度使。

translations.literal: He was appointed military governor of Yan-Hai-Yi-Mi.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military governor of Yan, Hai, Yi, and Mi.

sentences.zh: 遷義成軍，檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He was moved to the Yicheng army and made acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred to Yicheng and was named acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 入拜右金吾衛大將軍，復節度邠寧。

translations.literal: He entered court as Grand General of the Right Imperial Guards and again governed Binning.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Grand General of the Right Imperial Guards and once more took Binning.

sentences.zh: 先是，虜多以盛秋犯邊，承簡請屯寧州以制其侵。

translations.literal: Before this the barbarians often raided in the height of autumn; Chengjian asked to station troops at Ningzhou to check their incursions.
translations.idiomatic: The nomads had been striking in late autumn; he asked to garrison Ningzhou to block them.

sentences.zh: 屬疾還朝，道卒，贈司空，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: He fell ill on the road while returning to court and died; posthumously he was made Grand Master of Works and given the posthumous title Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Illness overtook him on the journey home; he was posthumously made Grand Master of Works and titled Reverent.

sentences.zh: 崇文孫駢，自有傳。

translations.literal: Chongwen's grandson Pian has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwen's grandson Pian is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 伊慎，字寡悔，兗州人。

translations.literal: Yi Shen, styled Guahuai, was a man of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Shen, styled Guahuai, came from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 通《春秋》、《戰國策》、天官、五行書，用善射為折沖都尉。

translations.literal: He mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Stratagems of the Warring States, works on celestial offices and the Five Phases, and by skill in archery became Vanquisher Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Warring States Annals, astronomy, and the Five Phases, and won appointment as Vanquisher Colonel through his archery.

sentences.zh: 喪母，將合葬而不知父墓，晝夜哭，夢若有導者；

translations.literal: When his mother died he wished to bury her with his father but did not know his father's grave; day and night he wept, and in dreams there seemed to be one who guided him;
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his mother, he sought to bury her beside his father but could not find the tomb; he wept day and night until dreams seemed to lead him;

sentences.zh: 既發之，舊誌可按也，乃得葬。

translations.literal: when they opened the ground the old record could be matched, and the burial was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: when they dug, an old record matched the spot, and the burial was done.

sentences.zh: 江西路嗣恭討哥舒晃，以慎為先鋒。

translations.literal: When Lu Sichong of Jiangxi campaigned against Geshu Huang, he made Shen the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sichong of Jiangxi, campaigning against Geshu Huang, put Shen in the van.

sentences.zh: 疾戰破賊，斬首三千級，下韶州。

translations.literal: In fierce fighting he broke the rebels, beheaded three thousand, and took Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He fought hard, routed the enemy, took three thousand heads, and captured Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 戰把江口，水湍駛，乃為桴，寘薪焉，乘風縱火，賊焚且溺不可計，與諸將追斬晃泔溪。

translations.literal: At the battle of Bajiangkou the current ran swift; he made rafts, loaded them with fuel, and sent them downwind with fire; the rebels burned and drowned beyond counting, and with the other generals he pursued and slew Huang at Gan Stream.
translations.idiomatic: At Bajiangkou the river ran fast; he built rafts piled with fuel, loosed them on the wind with fire, and the enemy burned and drowned in untold numbers; then he and his colleagues ran Huang down and killed him at Gan Stream.

sentences.zh: 授連州長史，知團練副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief administrator of Lianzhou and acting deputy commissioner of the militia.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief administrator of Lianzhou and acting militia deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三遷江州別駕。

translations.literal: After three promotions he was vice-prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Three promotions later he was vice-prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 討梁崇義也，慎以江西牙兵屬李希烈，希烈署漢南北兵馬使，不受，獨率所部破崇義於蠻水，效俘三萬。

translations.literal: When Liang Chongyi was attacked, Shen led the Jiangxi guard troops under Li Xilie; Xilie appointed him commander of Han's northern and southern forces, but he would not accept and led only his own men to defeat Chongyi at Manshui, presenting thirty thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Liang Chongyi, Shen was attached to Li Xilie with Jiangxi troops; Xilie tried to give him command of the Han armies, but he refused, led his own detachment alone, smashed Chongyi at Manshui, and sent up thirty thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 襄、漢平，功多。

translations.literal: When Xiang and Han were pacified his merit was great.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangyang and Hanzhong were secured, his service stood high.

sentences.zh: 希烈愛其材，數饋遺，欲縻止之，卒以計免。

translations.literal: Xilie admired his talent and repeatedly sent gifts, wishing to detain him, but in the end Shen escaped by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie prized him, showered him with gifts, and tried to keep him, yet Shen slipped away by a ruse.

sentences.zh: 明年，希烈果反。

translations.literal: The next year Xilie did indeed rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Xilie rebelled as Shen had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 嗣曹王臯至鐘陵，得而壯之，拔為大將。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Cao, Li Gao, reached Zhongling he obtained Shen and was impressed, and promoted him to a chief general.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Li Gao of Cao, reaching Zhongling, took Shen into favor and made him a senior commander.

sentences.zh: 希烈恐為臯所任，遺以七屬甲，詐為慎書，行反間。

translations.literal: Xilie feared Shen would be trusted by Gao and sent him a seven-layer coat of mail, forging Shen's hand in a letter to sow discord.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Gao would rely on Shen, Xilie sent a seven-layer mail coat and a forged letter in Shen's name to sow distrust.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使即軍中斬之，臯表列其誣，未報。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to execute him in the army; Gao memorialized the fraud, but no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered him executed in camp; Gao exposed the plot, yet no answer returned.

sentences.zh: 賊溯江徇地，臯授慎兵，勞而遣，與賊大戰，破之，收黃梅，次長平，殺賊將，斬級千餘，拔蔡山尤力。

translations.literal: The rebels advanced upriver seizing territory; Gao gave Shen troops, encouraged him, and sent him forth; he fought a great battle, broke them, recovered Huangmei, pressed to Changping, killed a rebel general, and took more than a thousand heads; at Mount Cai his effort was especially great.
translations.idiomatic: As rebels swept the river country Gao armed Shen, cheered him on, and let him strike; Shen won a great victory, retook Huangmei, reached Changping, slew a rebel commander with over a thousand heads, and did especially fierce work at Mount Cai.

sentences.zh: 遂下蘄州，即拜刺史，封南充郡王。

translations.literal: He then took Qizhou and was at once made its governor and enfeoffed Prince of Nanchong.
translations.idiomatic: He next captured Qizhou, was made its governor on the spot, and enfeoffed Prince of Nanchong.

sentences.zh: 天子在梁州，包佶轉東南財糧次蘄口，賊遣驍將杜少誠以兵萬人遏江道，不得西。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was at Liangzhou; Bao Ji was moving southeastern grain and funds to Qikou, and the rebels sent the fierce general Du Shaoqing with ten thousand men to block the river route so nothing could pass west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sheltered at Liangzhou; Bao Ji was shipping grain from the southeast to Qikou when Du Shaoqing barred the river with ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 慎選士七千，列三屯相望，偃旗以待。

translations.literal: Shen chose seven thousand men and set three camps in sight of one another, lowering banners to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Shen picked seven thousand men, pitched three camps within view of each other, and hid their banners in ambush.

sentences.zh: 少誠分圍之，未合，慎自中屯鼓之，諸屯悉出奮擊，賊亂，少誠走，斬別將許少華，封其屍為京冢，漕無留艱。

translations.literal: Shaoqing divided his force to surround them; before the ring closed Shen himself drummed the attack from the middle camp; all camps rushed out and struck; the rebels were thrown into disorder, Shaoqing fled, the deputy Xu Shaohua was beheaded, his corpse was sealed and sent to the capital as a trophy, and the transport route was never again blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqing split his men to encircle them; before the noose shut Shen drummed from the center and every camp surged forward; the enemy broke, Shaoqing ran, Xu Shaohua was killed and his body sent to the capital, and the grain route stayed open.

sentences.zh: 進圍安州，希烈之甥劉戒虛以兵八千來援，慎逆擊於應山，禽之，示城下，州開門降。

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Anzhou; Xilie's nephew Liu Jie led eight thousand men to the relief; Shen met them at Yingshan, captured Jie, and displayed him below the walls; the city opened its gates and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Anzhou; Liu Jie, Xilie's nephew, came with eight thousand; Shen met him at Yingshan, took him alive, showed him under the walls, and Anzhou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 以功為安州刺史，實封百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made governor of Anzhou with a substantive fief of a hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with the governorship of Anzhou and a fief of a hundred households.

sentences.zh: 改隋州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 戰厲鄉，斬首五千級，喻降李惠登，即薦惠登為刺史。

translations.literal: At the battle of Lixiang he beheaded five thousand; he persuaded Li Huideng to submit and at once recommended Huideng as governor.
translations.idiomatic: At Lixiang he took five thousand heads, won Li Huideng over, and immediately recommended him for governor.

sentences.zh: 拜慎安、黃州節度使。

translations.literal: Shen was appointed military governor of An and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military governor of An and Huang.

sentences.zh: 吳少誠反，詔領步騎五千兼統荊南、湖南、江西兵，當一面，遇賊於三州港，營義陽，戰於申，斬首數千，加檢校刑部尚書。

translations.literal: When Wu Shaocheng rebelled, an edict put him at the head of five thousand foot and horse and also in command of the Jingnan, Hunan, and Jiangxi forces on one front; he met the rebels at Sanzhou Harbor, camped at Yiyang, fought at Shen, and beheaded several thousand; he was made acting Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaocheng rose; Shen was given five thousand infantry and cavalry and overall command of troops from Jingnan, Hunan, and Jiangxi; at Sanzhou Harbor and Yiyang he cut down thousands and was made acting Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，詔安、黃為奉義軍，即為奉義節度。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan an edict made An and Huang the Fengyi army, and he became Fengyi military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenyuan An and Huang were renamed the Fengyi command, and he became its governor.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，以兵付其子宥，身入朝，拜尚書右僕射，改金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne Shen handed his troops to his son You and entered court himself, was made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and then Grand General of the Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianzong's accession he gave his army to his son You, came to court, became Right Vice Director, then Grand General of the Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 以錢三千萬賂宦人求帥河中，事暴，帝沒其半贓，貶右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He bribed eunuchs with thirty million cash to win the command of Hezhong; when the affair was exposed the emperor confiscated half the bribe and demoted him to general of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to buy the Hezhong command with thirty million cash; caught, he lost half the sum and was demoted to the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 明年，念舊勞，復檢校右僕射兼右衛上將軍。

translations.literal: The next year, remembering his old service, he was again made acting Right Vice Director and senior general of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, for past merit, he was restored as acting Right Vice Director and senior Right Guard general.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保，謚曰壯繆。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Stalwart but Erring.
translations.idiomatic: He died, was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and titled Stalwart but Erring.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，盜發其墓，賜絹二百修瘞雲。

translations.literal: In Qianfu robbers opened his tomb; two hundred bolts of silk were granted to repair the burial mound.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfu tomb robbers broke into his grave; the court granted two hundred bolts of silk to restore the mound.

sentences.zh: 朱忠亮，字仁輔，汴州浚儀人。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhongliang, styled Renfu, was a man of Junyi in Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhongliang, styled Renfu, came from Junyi in Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉明經不中，往事昭義節度使薛嵩為裨將，屯普潤，開田峙糧，以功擢太子賓客。

translations.literal: He sat for the classics examination and failed, then served Xue Song, military governor of Zhaoyi, as a staff officer, garrisoned at Puyuan, opened fields and stored grain, and by merit was raised to Household Companion of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Failing the classics exam, he joined Xue Song of Zhaoyi as a staff officer, garrisoned Puyuan, developed farmland and granaries, and was promoted to Household Companion of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 朱泚亂，率麾下四十騎至奉天，封東陽郡王，為「定難功臣」。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled he led forty horsemen to Fengtian, was enfeoffed Prince of Dongyang, and styled a "meritorious minister who settled disaster."
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's revolt he rode in with forty men to Fengtian, was made Prince of Dongyang, and hailed as a minister who quelled calamity.

sentences.zh: 扈狩梁州，為賊鈔獲，系長安獄。

translations.literal: He followed the hunt to Liangzhou, was captured in a rebel raid, and was imprisoned in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the court to Liangzhou, was taken in a rebel raid, and held in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 賊平，李晟釋之，奏隸本軍，累遷定平軍使。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified Li Sheng released him, memorialized that he be attached to the original army, and he rose through posts to commander of the Dingping army.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion Li Sheng freed him, had him restored to service, and he advanced to commander of the Dingping army.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，加御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne he was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianzong's accession he became Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 涇州將楊琦謀拒詔為亂，方集諸校計事，屋壞，琦壓死，乃授忠亮涇原四鎮節度使。

translations.literal: The Jingzhou officer Yang Qi plotted to defy the edict and rebel; just as he was gathering the officers to plan, the roof collapsed and Qi was crushed to death; thereupon Zhongliang was made military governor of the four Jingyuan commands.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qi of Jingzhou plotted rebellion; while he met his officers the roof fell and crushed him; Zhongliang was then made governor of the four Jingyuan commands.

sentences.zh: 本名士明，至是賜今名。

translations.literal: His original name was Shiming; at this time he was given his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Born Shiming, he now received his present name from the throne.

sentences.zh: 隱核軍籍，得竄名者三千人，歲收乾沒十萬緡。

translations.literal: He secretly audited the military rolls and found three thousand false names; each year he collected a hundred thousand strings in graft.
translations.idiomatic: Auditing the rolls in secret he found three thousand phantom soldiers and collected a hundred thousand strings a year in illicit fees.

sentences.zh: 吏白耄卒不任戰者可罷，答曰：「古於老馬不棄，況戰士乎？」

translations.literal: The clerks reported that old soldiers unfit for war could be dismissed; he answered, "In antiquity they did not cast aside old horses — how much less fighting men?"
translations.idiomatic: Clerks said aged soldiers unfit for battle might be discharged; he replied, "The ancients kept old horses — shall we discard warriors?

sentences.zh: 聞者莫不感奮。

translations.literal: Those who heard were none who were not stirred to ardor.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, none failed to take fire.

sentences.zh: 涇俗舊多賣子，忠亮以財贖免者前後數百。

translations.literal: The custom of Jing was to sell children often; Zhongliang used his wealth to redeem several hundred before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Jing customarily sold children; Zhongliang ransomed several hundred with his own funds.

sentences.zh: 築潘原城有勞，改封丹陽。

translations.literal: He had merit in building Panyuan city and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: For building Panyuan Fort he was re-enfeoffed Prince of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰靈。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and given the posthumous title Spirited.
translations.idiomatic: He died, was posthumously made Right Vice Director, and titled Spirited.

sentences.zh: 劉昌裔，字光後，太原陽曲人。

translations.literal: Liu Changyi, styled Guanghou, was a man of Yangqu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changyi, styled Guanghou, came from Yangqu in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 幼重遲不好戲，常若有所思度。

translations.literal: As a child he was grave and slow and did not care for play, always seeming to measure something in thought.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was solemn and unhurried, shunning games as though always weighing some distant matter.

sentences.zh: 及壯，策說邊將不售，去入蜀。

translations.literal: When grown he offered stratagems to frontier generals but found no buyer, and went into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he peddled plans to border generals without success and withdrew into Shu.

sentences.zh: 楊惠琳亂，昌裔說之。

translations.literal: When Yang Huilin rebelled, Changyi persuaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Huilin rose, Changyi won him over.

sentences.zh: 子琳順命，拜瀘州刺史，署昌裔州佐。

translations.literal: Huilin obeyed the command; Changyi was made governor of Luzhou and appointed a prefectural aide.
translations.idiomatic: Huilin submitted; Changyi was made governor of Luzhou and kept on as staff aide.

sentences.zh: 子琳死，客河朔間。

translations.literal: When Huilin died, Changyi wandered as a guest in the Yellow River north.
translations.idiomatic: After Huilin's death he wandered north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 曲環方攻濮州，表為判官。

translations.literal: When Qu Huan was attacking Puzhou he was recommended as judge on the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Huan, besieging Puzhou, took him on as staff judge.

sentences.zh: 為環檄李納，剴曉大誼，環上其稿，德宗異之。

translations.literal: For Huan he drafted a proclamation to Li Na, earnestly setting forth great principle; Huan sent up the draft and Dezong was struck by it.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote for Huan a manifesto to Li Na, arguing the larger right; Huan forwarded it and Dezong marveled.

sentences.zh: 環領陳許軍，又從府遷。

translations.literal: When Huan took command of the Chenxu army Changyi moved with the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan took the Chenxu command Changyi went with him.

sentences.zh: 累進營田副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to deputy commissioner of military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to deputy commissioner of military colonies.

sentences.zh: 環卒，上官涚知後務，吳少誠引兵薄城，涚欲遁去，昌裔止曰：「受詔而守，死其職也。

translations.literal: When Huan died Shangguan Ze took charge of rear affairs; Wu Shaocheng led troops to press the city; Ze wished to flee, but Changyi stopped him, saying, "You received an edict to hold this place — to die is your duty.
translations.idiomatic: Huan died; Shangguan Ze held headquarters; Wu Shaocheng pressed the walls; Ze meant to run, but Changyi said, "You were ordered to hold this city — death is the office.

sentences.zh: 況士馬完奮，足支賊。

translations.literal: Moreover men and horses are intact and eager — enough to withstand the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Our men and horses are whole and keen — enough to face them.

sentences.zh: 若堅壁不戰七日，賊氣必衰，我以全制之可也。」

translations.literal: If you hold the walls and do not fight for seven days the rebels' spirit will surely decline, and with our full strength we can master them.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the walls seven days without battle and their ardor will fade; then strike with full force and you will master them.

sentences.zh: 涚許諾。

translations.literal: Ze agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Ze consented.

sentences.zh: 賊攻堞壞，不得修。

translations.literal: The rebels battered the parapet until it could not be repaired.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy smashed the battlements beyond quick repair.

sentences.zh: 昌裔密造飛棚聯柵，即募突將千人鑿城以出，擊賊走之。

translations.literal: Changyi secretly built flying sheds linked into palisades, then recruited a thousand shock troops who tunneled out of the city and struck; the rebels were driven off.
translations.idiomatic: Changyi secretly built flying galleries and linked stockades, then raised a thousand storm troops who broke out through a tunnel and routed the besiegers.

sentences.zh: 比還，柵已立，守陴遂安。

translations.literal: Before they returned the palisade was already standing, and defense on the walls was secure.
translations.idiomatic: They returned to find the palisade finished and the ramparts safe.

sentences.zh: 兵馬使安國寧謀應賊，昌裔以計斬之；

translations.literal: The horse commander An Guoning plotted to join the rebels; Changyi killed him by stratagem;
translations.idiomatic: An Guoning, horse commander, plotted treason; Changyi destroyed him by a ruse;

sentences.zh: 召其麾下千人為饗，人賞二縑，乃伏兵於道，令「持縑者斬」，一不能脫，賊聞解去。

translations.literal: he summoned Guoning's thousand men to a feast, gave each two bolts of silk, then set ambush on the road with the order "Cut down whoever holds silk" — not one escaped; hearing this, the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: he feasted Guoning's thousand men, gave each two bolts of silk, then ambushed the road with orders to kill anyone still holding silk — none escaped; the enemy heard and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 以功擢涚陳許節度使，昌裔陳州刺史。

translations.literal: For his merit Ze was advanced to military governor of Chenxu and Changyi was made governor of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Ze became military governor of Chenxu and Changyi governor of Chen.

sentences.zh: 韓全義敗於溵水，引軍走陳，求入保，昌裔登陴揖曰：「天子命君討蔡，何為來陳？

translations.literal: When Han Quanyi was defeated on the Yin he led his army to Chen seeking refuge; Changyi mounted the wall and bowed, saying, "The Son of Heaven ordered you to attack Cai — why have you come to Chen?
translations.idiomatic: Han Quanyi, beaten on the Yin, fled to Chen for shelter; Changyi stood on the wall and bowed: "The throne sent you against Cai — why enter Chen?

sentences.zh: 且賊不敢至我城下，君其舍外無恐。」

translations.literal: Moreover the rebels dare not come below our walls; my lord may camp outside without fear.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels will not dare our walls; camp outside without fear.

sentences.zh: 明日，從十餘騎持牛酒抵全義營勞軍，全義不自意，迎拜嘆服。

translations.literal: The next day with a dozen riders he brought oxen and wine to Quanyi's camp to comfort the army; Quanyi had not expected it and came forward bowing in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he rode out with a dozen men, oxen and wine to Quanyi's camp; Quanyi, astonished, met him with bows of respect.

sentences.zh: 改陳許行軍司馬。

translations.literal: He was changed to campaigning staff marshal of Chenxu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made campaigning staff marshal of Chenxu.

sentences.zh: 涚卒，軍中推昌裔，有詔檢校工部尚書，代節度。

translations.literal: When Ze died the army pushed Changyi; an edict named him acting Minister of Works and military governor in Ze's place.
translations.idiomatic: Ze died; the troops acclaimed Changyi; the court made him acting Minister of Works and governor.

sentences.zh: 命境上吏不得犯蔡人，少誠吏有來犯者，捕得縛送，使自治之。

translations.literal: He ordered border officials not to molest men of Cai; when Shaocheng's officers came to violate the border they were seized and bound and sent back for Shaocheng to punish himself.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade his borders to harm Cai subjects; Shaocheng's men who crossed were caught, bound, and returned for Shaocheng's own justice.

sentences.zh: 少誠慚其軍，亦禁境上暴掠者。

translations.literal: Shaocheng was ashamed before his army and likewise forbade violent plunder on the border.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Shaocheng forbade his own men to plunder across the line.

sentences.zh: 封彭城郡公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was created Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 元和八年，大水壞廬舍，溺居人，以檢校尚書左僕射兼左龍武統軍召還京師。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanhe great floods destroyed houses and drowned inhabitants; he was summoned to the capital as acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and also commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 8 floods wrecked homes and drowned people; he was recalled as acting Left Vice Director and commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 始，憲宗惡昌裔自立，欲召之而重生變，宰相李吉甫曰：「陛下乘人心愁苦可召也。」

translations.literal: At first Xianzong disliked that Changyi had made himself master and wished to summon him but feared fresh trouble; the chief minister Li Jifu said, "Your Majesty may summon him while the people's hearts are still sore.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong had resented Changyi's self-appointment and hesitated to recall him lest trouble follow; Li Jifu said, "Summon him while the people still ache from flood and hardship.

sentences.zh: 遂以韓臯代之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Han Gao replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gao was sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 至長樂驛，知帝意，因稱風眩臥第。

translations.literal: At Changle post station he learned the emperor's mind and thereupon claimed vertigo and lay sick at home.
translations.idiomatic: At Changle post he sensed the emperor's intent, claimed dizziness, and kept to his house.

sentences.zh: 歲中卒，贈潞州大都督，謚曰威。

translations.literal: Within the year he died; posthumously he was made Grand Governor of Luzhou and given the posthumous title Majestic.
translations.idiomatic: He died within the year, was posthumously made Grand Governor of Luzhou, and titled Majestic.

sentences.zh: 範希朝，字致君，河中虞鄉人。

translations.literal: Fan Xichao, styled Zhijun, was a man of Yuxiang in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xichao, styled Zhijun, came from Yuxiang in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 初從邠寧軍為別將，事節度使韓遊瑰。

translations.literal: At first he followed the Binning army as a separate commander and served the military governor Han Yougui.
translations.idiomatic: He began in the Binning army as a separate commander under Han Yougui.

sentences.zh: 德宗在奉天，以戰守功累兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Dezong was at Fengtian he was repeatedly promoted for merit in defense and attack until he also held the post of Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengtian he won repeated promotion for defense and assault until he held the censor's seal.

sentences.zh: 治軍整毅，遊瑰畏其才，將伺隙殺之，希朝懼，奔鳳翔。

translations.literal: He governed troops with stern discipline; Yougui feared his talent and was about to find a pretext to kill him; Xichao was afraid and fled to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His camps were iron-hard; Yougui feared him and plotted his death; Xichao fled to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，召寘左神策軍。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and summoned him to the Left Divine Strategy Army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and placed him in the Left Divine Strategy Army.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，以遊瑰政無狀，使代之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan, because Yougui's government was disorderly, Xichao was sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 4, Yougui's rule having failed, Xichao was sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 希朝曰：「始偪而來，終代其任，非所以防覬覦、安反仄也。」

translations.literal: Xichao said, "At first I was driven here by force, and in the end I replace his post — this is not how to guard against covetous eyes and settle restless hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Xichao said, "I was forced here at sword's point and now inherit his seat — that will not quiet envy or fear.

sentences.zh: 固讓左金吾衛將軍張獻甫。

translations.literal: He firmly yielded to Zhang Xianfu, general of the Left Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly yielded the post to Zhang Xianfu of the Left Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 軍中憚獻甫嚴，以兵脅監軍使請於帝，必得希朝乃止。

translations.literal: The army feared Xianfu's severity and with arms compelled the army supervisor to petition the emperor that only if Xichao were obtained would they stop.
translations.idiomatic: The troops, dreading Xianfu's harshness, threatened the supervisor until the throne gave them Xichao.

sentences.zh: 詔拜寧州刺史、邠寧節度副使，俾佐獻甫。

translations.literal: An edict made him governor of Ningzhou and deputy military governor of Binning to assist Xianfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Ningzhou and deputy governor of Binning to aid Xianfu.

sentences.zh: 俄遷振武節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to military governor of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became military governor of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 部有党項、室韋雜居，暴掠放肆，日入慝作，謂之「刮城門」。

translations.literal: In his command Dangxiang and Shiwei lived mixed together, plundering wildly; daily they entered to do evil, which was called "scraping the city gate."
translations.idiomatic: Dangxiang and Shiwei lived intermingled, raiding at will in what was called "scraping the gate."

sentences.zh: 希朝度要害置屯保，斥邏嚴密，鄙民以安。

translations.literal: Xichao judged the strategic points and set garrison forts, tightened border patrols, and the rustic people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified the vital points, tightened patrols, and the countryside grew calm.

sentences.zh: 至小竊取亦殺無赦，虜人憚伏，相謂曰：「是必張光晟紿姓名來也！」

translations.literal: Even petty theft he punished with death without pardon; the barbarians submitted in fear and said to one another, "This must be Zhang Guangcheng cheating us with a false name!
translations.idiomatic: Petty thieves he killed without mercy; the tribesmen quaked and whispered, "Surely this is Zhang Guangcheng under a false name!

sentences.zh: 邊州每長帥至，必效橐它駿馬，雖甚廉者猶受之，以結其歡。

translations.literal: On the frontier whenever a new commander came the tribes always presented Bactrian camels and fine horses — even the very upright usually accepted, to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a new commander arrived the tribes offered Bactrian camels and swift horses — even honest men took them to win goodwill.

sentences.zh: 希朝一不納。

translations.literal: Xichao accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Xichao refused every gift.

sentences.zh: 積十四年，虜保塞不敢橫。

translations.literal: For fourteen years the barbarians kept the passes and dared not run riot.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen years the nomads held the passes and dared not raid.

sentences.zh: 初，單于城池不樹，希朝命蒔柳，數歲成林。

translations.literal: At first the Chanyu city had no trees; Xichao ordered willows planted, and in several years they became a forest.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu city had been treeless; he planted willows until a forest stood.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，請朝。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan he requested audience.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenyuan he asked to come to court.

sentences.zh: 時諸鎮不以事自述職者，希朝而已。

translations.literal: At that time among the various commands none came to court to report affairs except Xichao alone.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the frontier commands only Xichao still came to report in person.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，拜右金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and made him Grand General of the Right Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and made him Grand General of the Right Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 王叔文用事，謂其易制，用為右神策統軍，充左右神策京西諸城鎮行營節度使，屯奉天，以韓泰為副，因欲使泰代之。

translations.literal: When Wang Shuwen held power he thought Xichao easy to control and used him as commander of the Right Divine Strategy Army and commissioner of the western capital garrisons, garrisoning Fengtian, with Han Tai as deputy, intending that Tai replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen, thinking him pliable, made him commander of the Right Divine Strategy Army and commissioner of the western capital garrisons at Fengtian, with Han Tai as deputy meant to supplant him.

sentences.zh: 會不能得神策軍而罷。

translations.literal: In the event he could not win the Divine Strategy army and the plan was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to win the Divine Strategy troops and the scheme collapsed.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，檢校尚書左僕射，復為右金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne he was made acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and again Grand General of the Right Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianzong's accession he became acting Left Vice Director and again Grand General of the Right Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校司空，出為朔方靈鹽節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting Grand Master of Works and sent out as military governor of Shuofang, Ling, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was acting Grand Master of Works and governor of Shuofang, Ling, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 遷河東，率師討王承宗，敗之木刀溝，然老病，不能有大功。

translations.literal: He was moved to Hedong and led troops against Wang Chengzong; he defeated him at Mudao Gully, but he was old and ill and could not achieve great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Hedong he marched against Wang Chengzong, beat him at Mudao Gully, yet age and sickness kept him from greater glory.

sentences.zh: 還朝，改左龍武統軍，以太子太保致仕。

translations.literal: Returning to court he was changed to commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard and retired as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he commanded the Left Dragon Martial Guard and retired as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太師，謚忠武，改曰宣武。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Loyal Martial, later changed to Proclaiming Martial.
translations.idiomatic: He died, was posthumously Grand Preceptor, first titled Loyal Martial, later Proclaiming Martial.

sentences.zh: 希朝號當世善將，或比之趙充國。

translations.literal: Xichao was called the good general of his age; some compared him to Zhao Chongguo.
translations.idiomatic: Men called him the finest general of the age; some likened him to Zhao Chongguo.

sentences.zh: 在朔方時，招突厥別部沙陀千落眾萬餘有之，其後用沙陀戰者，所至有功。

translations.literal: While at Shuofang he recruited more than ten thousand households of the Shatuo Turks, a separate branch; afterward wherever Shatuo troops fought they achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: At Shuofang he gathered ten thousand-odd Shatuo households; thereafter Shatuo fighters won merit wherever they were sent.

sentences.zh: 王鍔，字昆吾，自言太原人。

translations.literal: Wang E, styled Kunwu, said of himself that he was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E, styled Kunwu, claimed Taiyuan as his home.

sentences.zh: 始隸湖南團練府為裨將。

translations.literal: At first he served the Hunan training command as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a staff officer in the Hunan training command.

sentences.zh: 楊炎道潭，與語，異其才。

translations.literal: Yang Yan was directing Tanzhou and spoke with him; he marveled at his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan, touring Tanzhou, spoke with him and marveled at his mind.

sentences.zh: 嗣曹王臯為團練使，俾鍔誘降武岡叛將王國良，以功擢邵州刺史。

translations.literal: When Prince Li Gao of Cao became training commissioner he had E entice the Wugang rebel Wang Guoliang to submit; for this he was raised to governor of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Li Gao of Cao sent E to win over the Wugang rebel Wang Guoliang; for that he was made governor of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 臯之節度江西也，李希烈南侵，臯與鍔兵三千，使屯潯陽，而臯全軍臨九江，襲蘄州，遂以眾濟。

translations.literal: When Gao governed Jiangxi, Li Xilie invaded from the south; Gao and E with three thousand men were stationed at Xunyang while Gao with his whole army pressed Jiujiang, raided Qizhou, and then crossed with the host.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao held Jiangxi and Xilie struck south, E held Xunyang with three thousand while Gao took Jiujiang, raided Qizhou, and crossed in force.

sentences.zh: 表鍔江州刺史兼御史中丞，充都虞候。

translations.literal: He memorialized E as governor of Jiangzhou and concurrent Imperial Censor, and chief commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He made E governor of Jiangzhou, concurrent censor, and chief commandant.

sentences.zh: 鍔小心，善刺軍中情偽，事無細大，臯悉知之。

translations.literal: E was careful and skilled at probing the army's truth and falsehood; nothing large or small escaped Gao's knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: E was cautious and expert at reading the army's secrets; nothing, great or small, was hidden from Gao.

sentences.zh: 因推以腹心，雖家人燕居或預焉。

translations.literal: Therefore Gao advanced him to the inner heart; even at family gatherings E was sometimes present.
translations.idiomatic: Gao drew him into his inmost counsel; E was sometimes present even at family meals.

sentences.zh: 臯攻安州，使伊慎盛兵圍之，而遣鍔入城中約降，使殺不從者。

translations.literal: When Gao attacked Anzhou he had Yi Shen surround it with a strong force while he sent E into the city to arrange surrender and kill those who would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Besieging Anzhou Gao sent Shen with the main force and E into the city to negotiate surrender and kill the stubborn.

sentences.zh: 翌日城開，慎以賊降乃己功，不下鍔，鍔稱疾避之。

translations.literal: The next day the city opened; Shen thought the rebel surrender was his own merit and did not mention E; E claimed illness and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Shen claimed the credit and omitted E; E pleaded illness and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 臯為荊南節度使，欲署府少尹，而上佐鄙其人，乃復檄都虞候。

translations.literal: When Gao became military governor of Jingnan he wished to appoint E vice prefect of the headquarters, but the senior staff despised him, so he was again made chief commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Made governor of Jingnan Gao tried to name E vice prefect, but senior staff scorned him and E returned as commandant.

sentences.zh: 從臯朝京師，臯奏鍔文用雖不足，而它可試。

translations.literal: Following Gao to the capital, Gao memorialized that E's literary use was insufficient but other things might be tried.
translations.idiomatic: At court Gao said E lacked polish in letters but might be tested elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 德宗擢為鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: Dezong promoted him to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong raised him to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 先是，天寶末，西域朝貢酋長及安西、北庭校吏歲集京師者數千人，隴右既陷，不得歸，皆仰稟鴻臚禮賓，月四萬緡，凡四十年，名田養子孫如編民。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Tianbao, chieftains of the western regions who came to court and officers of Anxi and Beiting gathered each year in the capital by the thousands; after Longyou fell they could not return and all relied on the Honglu office for guests of honor, four ten-thousand strings a month — for forty years they registered fields and raised sons and grandsons like commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Since late Tianbao western chieftains and Anxi and Beiting officers had gathered yearly at court by the thousands; when Longyou fell they could not go home and lived forty years on Honglu stipends of forty thousand strings a month, buying land and raising families like common folk.

sentences.zh: 至是，鍔悉籍名王以下無慮四千人，畜馬二千，奏皆停給。

translations.literal: Now E fully registered all from kings by name downward, nearly four thousand persons, with two thousand horses, and memorialized that all stipends be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: E registered nearly four thousand titled foreigners and two thousand horses and petitioned to end every stipend.

sentences.zh: 宰相李泌盡以隸左右神策軍，以酋長署牙將，歲省五十萬緡。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Mi assigned them all to the Left and Right Divine Strategy armies, appointing chieftains as guard officers, saving five hundred thousand strings a year.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi attached them to the Divine Strategy armies as guard officers, saving five hundred thousand strings yearly.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其公，擢容管經略使。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his public spirit and promoted him to commissioner of Rongguan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his integrity and made him commissioner of Rongguan.

sentences.zh: 凡八年，溪落安之。

translations.literal: In eight years the stream tribes were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In eight years the hill tribes were pacified.

sentences.zh: 遷嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: He was moved to military governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 廣人與蠻雜處，地征薄，多牟利於市，鍔租其廛，榷所入與常賦埒，以為時進，裒其餘悉自入。

translations.literal: The people of Guang mingled with the barbarians; land tax was light and profit was mostly taken in the markets; E rented their stalls and monopolized the revenue until it equaled the regular tax, offered it as timely tribute, and put the remainder entirely in his own purse.
translations.idiomatic: In Guang, where locals and tribes mixed and land tax was thin, E taxed the market stalls until monopoly income matched regular levies, sent the surplus up as tribute, and kept the rest.

sentences.zh: 諸蕃舶至，盡有其稅，於是財蓄不貲，日十餘艘載皆犀象珠琲，與商賈雜出於境。

translations.literal: When foreign ships arrived he took all their duties; wealth piled beyond measure, and daily more than ten vessels laden with rhinoceros horn, ivory, and pearls left the border mixed with merchants.
translations.idiomatic: He seized every port duty; treasure beyond counting flowed out daily in ten or more ships of ivory and pearls mixed with traders.

sentences.zh: 數年，京師權家無不富鍔之財。

translations.literal: Within several years no powerful house in the capital was without wealth from E.
translations.idiomatic: Within years every great clan in the capital held wealth from E.

sentences.zh: 召為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to be Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使杜佑數請代，乃以鍔檢校兵部尚書為佑副，厚事佑以悅之，坐必就司馬聽事，不數日，遂代佑。

translations.literal: The Huainan military governor Du You repeatedly asked to be replaced; E was made acting Minister of War as You's deputy; he treated You lavishly to please him, and at every sitting he went to the marshal's office to hear business; within a few days he replaced You.
translations.idiomatic: Du You of Huainan begged relief; E was made acting Minister of War as his deputy, flattered him, sat daily in the marshal's office, and within days replaced him.

sentences.zh: 久之，入拜尚書左僕射，又檢校司徒，為河中節度使。

translations.literal: After a long while he entered court as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was again made acting Grand Master of Works, and became military governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Left Vice Director, acting Grand Master of Works, and governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 進兼太子太傅，徙河東。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and moved to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and transferred to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 河東自範希朝討鎮無功，兵才三萬，騎六百，府庫殘耗。

translations.literal: Hedong, since Fan Xichao's campaign against Zhen had failed, had only thirty thousand troops, six hundred horse, and treasuries exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong, after Fan Xichao's failed campaign against Zhen, held only thirty thousand men, six hundred horse, and empty coffers.

sentences.zh: 鍔能補完嗇費，未幾，兵至五萬，騎五千，財用豐余。

translations.literal: E could repair and husband expenses; in no long time troops reached fifty thousand, horse five thousand, and funds were ample.
translations.idiomatic: E repaired accounts and husbanded stores; soon he had fifty thousand soldiers, five thousand horse, and full treasuries.

sentences.zh: 會回鶻並摩尼師入朝，鍔欲示威武傾駭之，乃悉軍迎，廷列五十里，旗幟光鮮，戈鎧犀密。

translations.literal: When the Uighurs and Manichaean teachers entered court together, E wished to display martial might and overawe them; he met them with the whole army drawn up in ranks for fifty li, banners bright, armor and weapons dense.
translations.idiomatic: When Uighurs and Manichaean clergy came to court E paraded his whole army for fifty li, banners blazing, armor glittering.

sentences.zh: 回鶻恐，不敢仰視，鍔偃然受其禮。

translations.literal: The Uighurs were afraid and dared not look up; E calmly received their courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The Uighurs dared not raise their eyes; E received their obeisance at ease.

sentences.zh: 帝聞嘉之，即除檢校司空、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was pleased, and at once made him acting Grand Master of Works and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and at once made him acting Grand Master of Works and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 鍔自見居財多，且懼謗，納錢二千萬。

translations.literal: E himself saw that he held much wealth and feared slander; he presented twenty million cash.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his wealth and fearing envy, he tendered twenty million cash.

sentences.zh: 李絳奏言：「鍔雖有勞，然僉望不屬，恐天下議以為宰相可市而取。」

translations.literal: Li Jiang memorialized, saying, "Though E has merit, public expectation does not fall on him — I fear the realm will say that the office of councillor can be bought.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang wrote, "E has service, yet the realm does not look to him — men will say the council seat is for sale.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「鍔當太原殘破後，成雄富之治。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "After Taiyuan was broken E built a rich and strong government.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "After Taiyuan lay in ruins he made it rich and strong.

sentences.zh: 官爵所以待功，功之不圖，何以為勸？

translations.literal: Rank and office exist to await merit — if merit is not rewarded, what will encourage men?
translations.idiomatic: Office exists to reward merit — deny merit and who will strive?

sentences.zh: 王播所獻數萬萬，亦可以平章政事乎？」

translations.literal: Wang Bo presented tens of millions — may he too be made Grand Councillor?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo gave tens of millions — shall he be councillor too?

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉，謚曰魏。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Marshal and given the posthumous title of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He died, was posthumously made Grand Marshal, and titled Wei.

sentences.zh: 鍔初附太原王翃為從子，以婚閥自高。

translations.literal: At first E attached himself to Wang Hong of Taiyuan as a nephew and prided himself on marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: At first he clung to Wang Hong of Taiyuan as a nephew and boasted of noble kinship.

sentences.zh: 翃子弟亦藉鍔多得官。

translations.literal: Hong's sons and younger brothers also relied on E to gain many offices.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's kin likewise rode E's coat-tails into office.

sentences.zh: 又常讀《春秋》，自稱儒者，士頗笑之。

translations.literal: He also often read the Spring and Autumn Annals and called himself a Confucian; gentlemen mostly laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: He read the Spring and Autumn Annals and called himself a scholar; men laughed.

sentences.zh: 善任數持下，在淮南時，嘗得無名書，內靴中，俄取它書焚之，人信其無名者，異日因小罪，並以所告窮驗，示眾以神明。

translations.literal: He was skilled at holding subordinates through stratagem; in Huainan he once received an anonymous letter and hid it in his boot; soon he took another book and burned it, so men believed he had no anonymous accuser; later on a small crime he used what had been reported to investigate thoroughly and show the crowd his clairvoyance.
translations.idiomatic: Clever at ruling inferiors, he once hid an anonymous denunciation in his boot, then burned another book so all thought him unread; later on a petty fault he exposed the informer's charges and passed for omniscient.

sentences.zh: 性纖嗇，有所程作，雖碎瑣無所遺。

translations.literal: His nature was minute and stingy; in any undertaking, however trifling, nothing was wasted.
translations.idiomatic: He was miserly in the extreme; in the smallest task nothing was lost.

sentences.zh: 官曹簾壞，吏將易之，鍔取壞者付船坊以針箬。

translations.literal: When office curtains rotted the clerks would replace them; E took the ruined ones to the boat yard for patching with needle and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: When office curtains rotted clerks would replace them; E sent the rags to the boatyard to be patched.

sentences.zh: 每燕饗，輒錄其餘，賣之以收利。

translations.literal: At every banquet he recorded the leftovers and sold them for profit.
translations.idiomatic: After every feast he sold the leftovers for gain.

sentences.zh: 故鍔家錢遍天下。

translations.literal: Therefore E's household money spread through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Wang fortune reached every corner of the empire.

sentences.zh: 子稷，歷鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: His son Ji held the post of Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 鍔在藩，稷常留京師，視勢高下輕重以納貲焉。

translations.literal: While E was in the provinces Ji often stayed in the capital, gauging power high and low and taking bribes accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: While E governed the provinces Ji stayed in the capital, weighing influence and selling favors.

sentences.zh: 嘗請籍坊以廣第舍，作復垣洞穴，實金錢其中。

translations.literal: He once asked to register a ward to enlarge his mansion, built a double wall with tunnels, and stored gold and cash within.
translations.idiomatic: He sought a ward lot to expand his mansion, built double walls with tunnels, and filled them with gold.

sentences.zh: 鍔卒，奴告稷更遺占，沒所獻，裴度為言，乃論殺奴。

translations.literal: When E died a slave reported that Ji had seized more tribute; the presented goods were confiscated; Pei Du spoke for him, and only the slave was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: At E's death a slave accused Ji of seizing more tribute; the gifts were seized; Pei Du intervened and only the slave was executed.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年，用稷為德州刺史，悉金寶、媵侍以行。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changqing Ji was made governor of Dezhou and took all gold, jewels, and concubines with him.
translations.idiomatic: In Changqing 2 Ji went to Dezhou carrying every treasure and concubine.

sentences.zh: 節度使李全略利其貨，因軍亂殺稷，納其女為媵。

translations.literal: The military governor Li Quanlue coveted his wealth; he used army disorder to kill Ji and took his daughter as concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quanlue of the circuit coveted his wealth, stirred mutiny, killed Ji, and took his daughter.

sentences.zh: 開成中，滄州節度使劉約奏稷子叔泰生五歲，值全略亂，為郡人匿養，得不死。

translations.literal: In Kaicheng Liu Yue of Cangzhou memorialized that Ji's son Shutai, five years old when Quanlue's disorder came, was hidden and raised by the district and did not die.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng Liu Yue reported that Shutai, five when Quanlue rebelled, had been hidden and lived.

sentences.zh: 送叔泰京師，文宗憫焉，詔授九品官，使奉鍔祀。

translations.literal: Shutai was sent to the capital; Wenzong pitied him and ordered a ninth-rank office to maintain E's sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Shutai was sent to court; Wenzong pitied him and gave a ninth-rank post to tend E's rites.

sentences.zh: 孟元陽，史失其何所人。

translations.literal: Meng Yuanyang. The histories lose where he was from.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yuanyang — the histories do not record his birthplace.

sentences.zh: 起陳許軍中，以嚴整稱。

translations.literal: He rose in the Chenxu army and was known for stern order.
translations.idiomatic: He came up in the Chenxu army famed for harsh discipline.

sentences.zh: 曲環領節度使，時已為大將，使董作西華屯。

translations.literal: When Qu Huan held the command he was already a great general and was sent to oversee work at the Xihua colony.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qu Huan he was already a senior general and directed the Xihua colony.

sentences.zh: 盛夏，屩而立於塗，役休乃就舍，故田輒歲稔，而軍食常足。

translations.literal: In midsummer he stood in straw sandals on the road until the labor rested before he went to quarters; therefore the fields were often rich and army grain was always full.
translations.idiomatic: In summer heat he stood in straw sandals on the road until work ended; the fields prospered and the granaries stayed full.

sentences.zh: 環卒，吳少誠來寇，元陽嬰城守，圍甚急，然終不能傅城。

translations.literal: When Huan died Wu Shaocheng came to attack; Yuanyang held the city under siege, which was very pressing, yet in the end the enemy could not reach the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Huan died; Shaocheng besieged him fiercely, yet never touched the walls.

sentences.zh: 韓全義敗五樓，列將多私去，獨元陽與神策將蘇元策、宣州將王幹以所部屯溵水，破賊二千，詔拜陳州刺史。

translations.literal: When Han Quanyi was defeated at Wulou many generals slipped away privately; only Yuanyang with the Divine Strategy general Su Yuanze and the Xuanzhou general Wang Gan held their detachments at the Yin and broke twenty thousand rebels; an edict made him governor of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: At Wulou most generals fled; only Yuanyang, Su Yuanze, and Wang Gan held the Yin line and slew twenty thousand; he was made governor of Chen.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，遷河陽節度使。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne he was moved to military governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianzong's accession he became governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 五年，盧從史敗，檢校尚書右僕射，徙帥昭義軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Lu Congshi was defeated; he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and transferred to command Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, after Lu Congshi's fall, he became acting Right Vice Director and governor of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 入為右羽林統軍，封趙國公。

translations.literal: He entered court as commander of the Right Feathered Forest Guard and was enfeoffed Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as commander of the Right Feathered Forest and was made Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 改右金吾大將軍，復拜統軍。

translations.literal: He was changed to Grand General of the Imperial Guards and again made commander of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: He became Grand General of the Imperial Guards and again commanded the guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王棲曜，濮州濮陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Qiyao was a man of Puyang in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiyao came from Puyang in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，尚衡裒義兵討賊，署牙將，徇兗、鄆諸縣下之，進牙前總管。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled Shang Heng gathered righteous troops to attack the rebels; Qiyao was appointed guard officer, subdued Yan and Yun counties, and was advanced to chief commander before the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose Shang Heng raised loyal troops; Qiyao served as guard officer, took the Yan and Yun counties, and became chief headquarters commander.

sentences.zh: 賊將邢超然守曹州，乘城指顧，棲曜曰：「彼可取也。」

translations.literal: The rebel general Xing Chaoran held Caozhou and gestured from the wall; Qiyao said, "He can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel Xing Chaoran held Caozhou and gestured from the wall; Qiyao said, "He is ours.

sentences.zh: 一矢殞之，遂拔曹州。

translations.literal: One arrow killed him, and Caozhou was taken.
translations.idiomatic: One arrow dropped him and Caozhou fell.

sentences.zh: 累授試金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly given the post of acting General of the Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly made acting General of the Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 袁晁亂浙東，御史中丞袁傪討之，表為偏將。

translations.literal: When Yuan Chao troubled Zhedong, Censor Yuan Zai campaigned against him and listed Qiyao as a flank general.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Chao ravaged Zhedong Yuan Zai campaigned against him and named Qiyao a flank commander.

sentences.zh: 與賊戰，日十餘遇，生禽晁，收州縣十六。

translations.literal: Fighting the rebels he met them more than ten times a day, captured Chao alive, and recovered sixteen prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He fought ten clashes a day, took Chao alive, and recovered sixteen districts.

sentences.zh: 授常州別駕、浙西都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice-prefect of Changzhou and commander of all Zhexi forces.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice-prefect of Changzhou and Zhexi commander.

sentences.zh: 時江介未定，詔內常侍馬日新以汴滑軍五千鎮之。

translations.literal: At that time the lower Yangtze was not yet settled; an edict sent the palace attendant Ma Rixin with five thousand Biansui troops to garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: The lower Yangtze was still unsettled; Ma Rixin was sent with five thousand Bian and Sui troops to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 中人暴橫，賊蕭廷蘭乘眾怨逐日新，劫其眾。

translations.literal: The eunuch was violent; the bandit Xiao Tinglan used popular hatred to drive Rixin off and seize his troops.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch bullied the people; Xiao Tinglan exploited their wrath, expelled Rixin, and stole his force.

sentences.zh: 棲曜方遊弈近郊，賊脅取之，與圍蘇州。

translations.literal: Qiyao was on patrol near the suburbs when the rebels seized him and made him join the siege of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyao was patrolling the suburbs when rebels seized him and forced him to besiege Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 棲曜乘賊怠，挺身登城，率城中兵出戰，賊眾大敗，遷試金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: Qiyao waited until the rebels slackened, leaped alone onto the wall, led the city troops out to fight, and the rebel host was utterly broken; he was moved up to acting Grand General of the Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When they slackened he vaulted the wall alone, led the garrison out, shattered the rebels, and was made acting Grand General of the Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 李靈曜反汴州，浙西觀察使李涵使提兵四千為河南掎角，有功。

translations.literal: When Li Lingyao rebelled at Bianzhou the Zhexi observer Li Han sent him with four thousand men as a pincer for Henan and he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Lingyao rebelled at Bianzhou Li Han sent him with four thousand men to pinch Henan from Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 李希烈陷汴州也，乘勝東略，次寧陵，將襲宋州。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie took Bianzhou he pressed east in victory, halted at Ningling, and was about to strike Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie, having taken Bianzhou, swept east, camped at Ningling, and meant to hit Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 浙西節度使韓滉使棲曜以強弩三千涉水，夜入寧陵，希烈不之知。

translations.literal: The Zhexi military governor Han Huang had Qiyao take three thousand strong crossbowmen across the water by night into Ningling without Xilie's knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang sent Qiyao with three thousand crossbowmen who crossed by night into Ningling unseen.

sentences.zh: 晨朝，矢集帳前，驚曰：「江淮弩士入矣！」

translations.literal: At morning audience arrows clustered before the tent; startled, Xilie said, "The crossbowmen of Jianghuai have entered!
translations.idiomatic: At dawn arrows thudded into his tent; Xilie cried, "The Jiang-Huai crossbowmen are here!

sentences.zh: 遂不敢東。

translations.literal: He did not dare go east.
translations.idiomatic: He dared not march east.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，拜左龍武大將軍，出為鄜坊節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he was made Grand General of the Left Dragon Martial Guard and sent out as military governor of Zhenfang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan he commanded the Left Dragon Martial Guard and governed Zhenfang.

sentences.zh: 十九年，卒，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰成。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died; posthumously he was made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and given the posthumous title Accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he died, was posthumously Right Vice Director, and titled Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 棲曜性謹厚，善騎射。

translations.literal: Qiyao was cautious and thick by nature and skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyao was steady and kindly and a master of mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 始將兵時，涉寇境，遇遊騎環合，乃規百步，立表而射，每射破的，虜相顧懼，引去。

translations.literal: When he first led troops he crossed into enemy territory and met roaming horsemen who ringed him; he measured a hundred paces, set a marker, and shot; every arrow struck the mark; the barbarians looked at one another in fear and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Early in command he rode into enemy country, was ringed by scouts, marked a hundred paces, and shot every bolt into the target; the nomads fled.

sentences.zh: 子茂元，少好學。

translations.literal: His son Maoyuan loved learning in youth.
translations.idiomatic: His son Maoyuan loved books as a youth.

sentences.zh: 德宗時上書自薦，擢試校書郎，改太子贊善大夫。

translations.literal: In Dezong's time he memorialized himself for recommendation and was raised to acting collator; he was changed to Senior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong he recommended himself and became acting collator, then Senior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 呂元膺留守東都，署防禦判官。

translations.literal: When Lü Yuanying held the eastern capital he was appointed defense judge.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yuanying at Luoyang made him defense judge.

sentences.zh: 淄青留邸卒謀亂，元膺率兵圍之，士無敢先者，茂元取一人斬之，眾乃進，賊遂出奔。

translations.literal: When the Ziqing lodge troops in the capital plotted disorder, Yuanying surrounded them with troops; none dared advance first; Maoyuan seized one man and beheaded him, and the host advanced; the rebels fled out.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziqing lodge troops plotted revolt Yuanying surrounded them; no one moved first; Maoyuan cut one man down and the host surged forward; the rebels ran.

sentences.zh: 累遷嶺南節度使，蠻落安之。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to military governor of Lingnan and the barbarian tribes were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to governor of Lingnan and pacified the tribes.

sentences.zh: 家積財，交煽權貴。

translations.literal: The family piled wealth and traded favors with the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: The house heaped riches and bought the mighty.

sentences.zh: 鄭註用事，遷涇原節度使。

translations.literal: When Zheng Zhu held power he was moved to military governor of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zheng Zhu he was made governor of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 註敗，悉出家貲餉兩軍，得不誅，封濮陽郡侯。

translations.literal: When Zhu fell he spent the household fortune to pay both armies and escaped execution; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu's fall would have killed him; he bought both armies with his fortune, survived, and was made Marquis of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 召為將作監，領陳許節度使，又徙河陽。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Director of Palace Construction and held the Chenxu command, then was moved to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of Palace Construction, governor of Chenxu, then Heyang.

sentences.zh: 討劉稹也，李德裕以茂元兵寡，詔王宰領陳許合義成兵援之，以河陰所貯兵械、內庫甲弓矢陌刀賜之。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhen was attacked Li Deyu thought Maoyuan's troops few; an edict had Wang Zai lead Chenxu and Yicheng troops to aid him and gave the stored arms of Heyin and the inner store's armor, bows, and pole blades.
