translations.idiomatic: Campaigning Liu Zhen, Deyu thought Maoyuan too weak; Wang Zai was sent with Chenxu and Yicheng troops and Heyin's armory.

sentences.zh: 會病，以宰兼河陽行營攻討使。

translations.literal: When illness came Wang Zai was made acting Heyang campaigning commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Falling ill he yielded the Heyang command to Wang Zai.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司徒，謚曰威。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Majestic.
translations.idiomatic: He died, was posthumously Grand Tutor, and titled Majestic.

sentences.zh: 劉昌，字公明，汴州開封人。

translations.literal: Liu Chang, styled Gongming, was a man of Kaifeng in Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang, styled Gongming, came from Kaifeng in Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 善騎射。

translations.literal: He was skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，從河南防禦使張介然討安祿山，授易州遂城府左果毅。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he followed the Henan defense commissioner Zhang Jieran to attack An Lushan and was appointed Left Commander of the Suifu Prefecture garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianbao he followed Zhang Jieran against An Lushan and was made Left Commander at Suifu.

sentences.zh: 史朝義兵圍宋州，城中食盡且降。

translations.literal: When Shi Chaoyi's troops besieged Songzhou the city ran out of food and was about to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chaoyi's army besieged Songzhou until food failed and surrender neared.

sentences.zh: 昌說刺史李岑曰：「李光弼在河陽，江淮足兵，勢必來援。

translations.literal: Chang persuaded the governor Li Cen, saying, "Li Guangbi is at Heyang and the Jiang-Huai have ample troops — relief is sure to come.
translations.idiomatic: Chang told Li Cen, "Guangbi holds Heyang and the southeast has armies — help will come.

sentences.zh: 今廩麹尚多，若屑以食，可支二十日，則救至。」

translations.literal: Now the granaries still hold much grain; if we grind it for food we can hold twenty days, and then rescue will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Grind the stores to flour and we can last twenty days until rescue.

sentences.zh: 岑聽之。

translations.literal: Cen listened.
translations.idiomatic: Cen agreed.

sentences.zh: 昌乃被鎧登城，以忠義諭賊，賊畏不敢攻。

translations.literal: Chang then donned armor, mounted the wall, and with righteous words warned the rebels; the rebels feared and did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: Chang armored, mounted the wall, and shamed the enemy with duty; they dared not press the assault.

sentences.zh: 俄而光弼援兵至，賊夜潰。

translations.literal: Soon Guangbi's relief arrived and the rebels fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guangbi came and the rebels stole away by night.

sentences.zh: 光弼聞其謀，召置軍中，將用之。

translations.literal: Guangbi heard of his plan and summoned him to the army intending to use him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi heard of the plan and called him to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 會光弼卒，還為宋州牙門將。

translations.literal: When Guangbi died he returned as guard officer at Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangbi died he returned to Song as guard officer.

sentences.zh: 李靈曜以汴州反，刺史李僧惠欲應之，昌請見，陳逆順計，且泣。

translations.literal: When Li Lingyao rebelled at Bianzhou the governor Li Sengyi wished to join him; Chang asked audience, set forth the calculus of loyalty and rebellion, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lingyao rebelled; Li Sengyi meant to join; Chang pleaded, argued treason and loyalty, and wept.

sentences.zh: 僧惠悟，即馳奏請自將討賊。

translations.literal: Sengyi came to himself and at once sent a hurried memorial asking to lead troops himself against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyi awoke and memorialized to lead the attack himself.

sentences.zh: 故靈曜失助，不得逞。

translations.literal: Therefore Lingyao lost aid and could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Lingyao lost help and could not win.

sentences.zh: 汴州平，李忠臣疾僧惠，攻殺之，昌遁去。

translations.literal: When Bianzhou was pacified Li Zhongchen hated Sengyi, attacked and killed him, and Chang fled.
translations.idiomatic: Bianzhou fell; Zhongchen killed Sengyi; Chang fled.

sentences.zh: 劉玄佐領宣武節度使，擢昌左廂兵馬使。

translations.literal: When Liu Xuanzuo took the Xuanwu command he raised Chang to commander of the left wing horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzuo made him commander of the left wing.

sentences.zh: 李納反，以偏師收考城，充行營諸軍馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: When Li Na rebelled he took Kaocheng with a detached force and was made campaigning commandant of all horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Na rebelled he took Kaocheng and became campaigning commandant of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 玄佐攻濮州，以昌攝刺史。

translations.literal: When Xuanzuo attacked Puzhou he had Chang act as governor.
translations.idiomatic: Besieging Puzhou Xuanzuo left Chang as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 李希烈取汴，玄佐別將高翼提精卒守襄邑，城陷，翼赴水死，江淮大震。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie took Bian, Xuanzuo's separate general Gao Yi with picked troops held Xiangyi; the city fell and Yi threw himself into the water and died; the Jiang-Huai were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie took Bian; Gao Yi held Xiangyi with elites; the city fell and Yi drowned; the southeast shook.

sentences.zh: 昌以兵三千守寧陵，希烈眾五萬攻之，昌掘塹以遏地道，相拒凡四十餘日，賊數敗，乃解圍去。

translations.literal: Chang with three thousand men held Ningling; Xilie's host of fifty thousand attacked; Chang dug trenches to block tunneling and resisted more than forty days; the rebels were repeatedly beaten and then lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Chang held Ningling with three thousand against fifty thousand, trenched against mines, fought forty days, broke the enemy, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 更攻陳州，昌從玄佐以浙西兵三萬救之。

translations.literal: Xilie again attacked Chenzhou; Chang followed Xuanzuo with thirty thousand Zhexi troops to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie struck Chenzhou; Chang marched with thirty thousand Zhexi men to save it.

sentences.zh: 西去陳五十里，昌薄其軍，大戰破之，禽賊將翟曜，希烈奔還蔡州。

translations.literal: Fifty li west of Chen he pressed the enemy army, fought a great battle and broke them, captured the rebel general Zhai Yao, and Xilie ran back to Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty li west of Chen he crushed the host, took Zhai Yao, and drove Xilie back to Cai.

sentences.zh: 加檢校工部尚書，累實封二百戶。

translations.literal: He was made acting Minister of Works with a cumulative substantive fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Minister of Works with two hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年入朝，詔以宣武兵八千北出五原。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan he entered court; an edict ordered eight thousand Xuanwu troops to march north out of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 3 he came to court; eight thousand Xuanwu troops were ordered north from Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 士卒有逗留沮事者，斬三百人乃行，舉軍慴伏。

translations.literal: When soldiers lingered and hindered the march he beheaded three hundred men and then marched; the whole army submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded three hundred stragglers and marched; the army trembled into order.

sentences.zh: 尋授京西行營節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed military governor of the western capital expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he governed the western capital expedition.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，改四鎮、北庭行營兼涇原節度。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was changed to commissioner of the four commands and northern court campaign and also military governor of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he held the four commands and northern court campaign and Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 七年，城平涼，開地二百里，扼彈箏峽。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he walled Pingliang and opened two hundred li of land, holding the Pipa Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he built Pingliang, opened two hundred li, and held Pipa Gorge.

sentences.zh: 又西築保定，扞青石嶺，凡七城二堡，旬日就。

translations.literal: He also built Baoding westward, guarding Qingshi Ridge — in all seven cities and two forts completed in ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Westward he built Baoding at Qingshi Ridge — seven cities and two forts in ten days.

sentences.zh: 以功檢校尚書右僕射，累封南川郡王。

translations.literal: For merit he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and repeatedly enfeoffed Prince of Nanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he became acting Right Vice Director and Prince of Nanchuan.

sentences.zh: 十四年，歸化堡軍亂，逐大將張國誠，詔昌經略。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Guihua Fort garrison mutinied, drove out the great general Zhang Guocheng, and an edict charged Chang to handle it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Guihua Fort mutinied and expelled Zhang Guocheng; Chang was sent to settle it.

sentences.zh: 昌入堡，誅數百人，復使國誠統之。

translations.literal: Chang entered the fort, executed several hundred men, and again set Guocheng in command.
translations.idiomatic: Chang entered, killed hundreds, and restored Guocheng.

sentences.zh: 昌在邊凡十五年，身率士墾田，三年而軍有羨食，兵械銳新，邊障妥寧。

translations.literal: Chang was on the frontier fifteen years in all; he personally led the men in farming the fields; in three years the army had surplus food, weapons were sharp and new, and the border was secure.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years on the border he led the men in farming; in three years granaries overflowed, arms gleamed, and the frontier was calm.

sentences.zh: 及感疾，詔赴京師。

translations.literal: When he fell ill an edict ordered him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Illness brought an order to court.

sentences.zh: 未行，卒，年六十五，贈司空。

translations.literal: Before he could go he died at sixty-five; posthumously he was made Grand Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-five before marching, and was posthumously Grand Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 初城平涼，當劫盟後，將士骸骨不藏，昌始命瘞之。

translations.literal: When Pingliang was first walled, after the captive-oath disaster the bones of officers and soldiers were not buried; Chang first ordered them interred.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingliang was raised, bones from the captive oath lay unburied; Chang buried them.

sentences.zh: 夕夢若詣昌厚謝者，昌具以聞。

translations.literal: At evening he dreamed as if those he had buried came to thank him thickly; Chang reported it fully.
translations.idiomatic: That night he dreamed the dead thanked him; he reported it.

sentences.zh: 德宗下詔哀痛，出衣數百稱，官為賽具，斂以棺槥，分建二冢，大將曰旌義冢，士曰懷忠冢，葬淺水原，詔翰林學士為銘識其所。

translations.literal: Dezong issued an edict of grief, sent out several hundred suits of clothing, had the officials prepare sacrificial goods, gathered them in coffins, and built two mounds — the great generals' Mound of Exalted Righteousness and the soldiers' Mound of Cherished Loyalty — buried at Qianshui Plain, and ordered Hanlin academicians to inscribe them.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong mourned, sent hundreds of garments, prepared rites, coffined the bones in two mounds — Exalted Righteousness for generals, Cherished Loyalty for soldiers — at Qianshui Plain with Hanlin inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 昌盛陳兵衛，具牢醴，率諸將素服臨之，邊兵莫不感泣。

translations.literal: Chang arrayed troops as guards, set out full offerings, and with the generals in plain dress attended; border soldiers none who did not weep.
translations.idiomatic: Chang drew up guards, offered full sacrifice, and stood with his generals in white; the border wept.

sentences.zh: 子士涇，尚云安公主，拜駙馬都尉，累遷少卿。

translations.literal: His son Shijing married Princess Yun'an, was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shijing married Princess Yun'an, became Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, and rose to vice minister.

sentences.zh: 家積財，內結權近。

translations.literal: The family amassed wealth and cultivated ties with those in power near the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The house heaped riches and courted power at court.

sentences.zh: 善胡琴，故得幸於貴人。

translations.literal: He was skilled on the barbarian lute and therefore won favor with the great.
translations.idiomatic: He played the barbarian lute and won favor among the mighty.

sentences.zh: 後遷太僕卿，給事中韋弘景等封還制書，以士涇交通近幸，不當居九卿。

translations.literal: Later he was moved to Grand Master of the Stud; the attendant Wei Hongjing and others returned the edict, saying Shijing trafficked with favorites and ought not hold one of the nine ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Made Grand Master of the Stud, Wei Hongjing returned the edict: Shijing traded on favorites and should not hold a ministry.

sentences.zh: 憲宗曰：「昌有功於邊，士涇又尚主，官少卿已十餘年，制書宜下。」

translations.literal: Xianzong said, "Chang had merit on the frontier and Shijing also married the princess; he has been vice minister more than ten years — let the edict go down."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong said, "Chang served the border; Shijing married the princess and has been vice minister ten years — issue the edict.

sentences.zh: 弘景等乃奉詔。

translations.literal: Hongjing and the others then obeyed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing and the others obeyed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：唐杜牧稱：「寧陵之圍解，劉玄佐召昌問曰：『君以孤城，用一當十，何以能守？』

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Tang Du Mu wrote, "When the siege of Ningling was lifted Liu Xuanzuo summoned Chang and asked, 'You held a lone city, one against ten — how could you defend it?
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal cites Du Mu: when Ningling was saved, Xuanzuo asked how one city held against ten.

sentences.zh: 昌泣曰：『始昌令：守陴內顧者斬。

translations.literal: Chang wept and said, 'From the first Chang ordered: whoever on the wall looked inward would be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Chang wept: he had ordered that anyone who looked inward from the wall would die.

sentences.zh: 昌孤甥張俊守西北，未嘗內顧，捽下斬之。

translations.literal: My lone nephew Zhang Jun held the northwest and never looked inward; I dragged him down and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Zhang Jun held the northwest and never looked inward; Chang dragged him down and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 士有死誌，故能守。』

translations.literal: The men had the will to die, therefore they could hold.
translations.idiomatic: The men willed death, and so the city held.

sentences.zh: 因伏地流涕，玄佐亦泣曰：『國家將富貴汝。』」

translations.literal: He then prostrated himself weeping, and Xuanzuo also wept and said, 'The state will enrich you.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself weeping; Xuanzuo wept too and said the state would enrich him.

sentences.zh: 史臣謂不然，且勒兵乘城與賊抗，所賴賞罰耳。

translations.literal: The historiographer says this is not so: to lead troops and mount the wall against the enemy relied on reward and punishment alone.
translations.idiomatic: The historian disagrees: defense rested on reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 今無罪而斬其甥，士心且離，不祥莫大焉。

translations.literal: Now to behead his nephew without crime — the soldiers' hearts would surely part; nothing more ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: To kill an innocent nephew would split the army — the worst omen.

sentences.zh: 寧好事者傅此以益其美？

translations.literal: Could lovers of strange tales have spread this to add to his glory?
translations.idiomatic: Did storytellers invent this to glorify him?

sentences.zh: 非昌誌也。

translations.literal: This was not Chang's intent.
translations.idiomatic: That was not Chang's way.

sentences.zh: 牧以為張巡、許遠陷睢陽，其名傳，昌全寧陵而事不得暴於世，寧牧未之思邪？

translations.literal: Did Mu think that Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan, trapped in Suiyang, won fame, while Chang fully held Ningling yet his affair could not be spread in the world — did Mu not reflect?
translations.idiomatic: Du Mu praised Zhang Xun at Suiyang yet ignored Chang at Ningling — had he forgotten?

sentences.zh: 趙昌，字洪祚，天水人。

translations.literal: Zhao Chang, styled Hongzuo, was a man of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang, styled Hongzuo, came from Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 始為昭義李承昭節度府屬，累遷虔州刺史。

translations.literal: At first he was a staff member under Li Chengzhao, military governor of Zhaoyi, and was promoted step by step to governor of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He began on Li Chengzhao's Zhaoyi staff and rose to governor of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 安南酋獠杜英翰叛，都護高正平以憂死，拜昌安南都護，夷落向化毋敢桀。

translations.literal: The chieftain Du Yinghan of Annan rebelled; Protector Gao Zhengping died of grief; Chang was made protector of Annan and the tribes turned to civilization and dared not be violent.
translations.idiomatic: When Annan's Du Yinghan rebelled and Protector Gao Zhengping died of grief, Chang was made protector; the tribes submitted and dared not rage.

sentences.zh: 居十年，足疾，請還朝，以兵部郎中裴泰代之，入為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: After ten years he had foot ailment and asked to return to court; Pei Tai of the Ministry of War replaced him; he entered as Director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later, lame, he asked to return; Pei Tai replaced him; he became Director of the National University.

sentences.zh: 未幾，州將逐泰，德宗召昌問狀，時年逾七十，占對精明，帝奇之，復拜安南都護。

translations.literal: Before long the prefectural troops drove Tai out; Dezong summoned Chang and asked the situation; he was past seventy yet answered sharply; the emperor marveled and again made him protector of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon troops expelled Tai; Dezong asked Chang, past seventy, who answered keenly; the emperor marveled and sent him back to Annan.

sentences.zh: 詔書至，人相賀，叛兵即定。

translations.literal: When the edict arrived the people congratulated one another and the mutinous soldiers at once settled.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict came the people rejoiced and the mutineers quieted.

sentences.zh: 憲宗初立，檢校戶部尚書，遷嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: When Xianzong first took the throne he was made acting Minister of Revenue and moved to military governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianzong's accession he became acting Minister of Revenue, then governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 降輯陬荒，以勞徙節荊南。

translations.literal: He pacified the distant tribes and was moved to Jingnan for his labor.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the far tribes and was transferred to Jingnan for his toil.

sentences.zh: 召入，再遷工部尚書、兼大理卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned in and twice promoted to Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Judge.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he twice rose to Minister of Works and Grand Judge.

sentences.zh: 出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 對麟德殿，趨拜強駃，帝訪其所以頤養。

translations.literal: At audience in Linde Hall his hurried bow was vigorous; the emperor asked how he kept himself so hale.
translations.idiomatic: At Linde Hall his bow was brisk; the emperor asked his secret of health.

sentences.zh: 遷太子少保。

translations.literal: He was moved to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He became Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十五，贈揚州大都督，謚曰成。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-five; posthumously he was made Grand Governor of Yangzhou and given the posthumous title Accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-five, was posthumously Grand Governor of Yangzhou, and titled Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 李景略，幽州良鄉人。

translations.literal: Li Jinglue, a man of Liangxiang in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinglue came from Liangxiang in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 父承悅，檀州刺史、密雲軍使。

translations.literal: His father Chengyue was governor of Tanzhou and commander of the Miyun army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengyue was governor of Tanzhou and commander of Miyun.

sentences.zh: 景略以蔭補幽州府功曹參軍。

translations.literal: Jinglue entered office by yin privilege as functionary of the Youzhou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: By yin privilege he became functionary of the Youzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，客河中，闔門讀書。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali he lodged at Hezhong and the whole household read books.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Dali he stayed at Hezhong and his household read.

sentences.zh: 李懷光為朔方節度使，署巡官。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang was military governor of Shuofang and appointed him touring officer.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang of Shuofang made him touring officer.

sentences.zh: 五原將張光殺其妻，以貲市獄，前後不能決，景略核實，論殺之。

translations.literal: The Wuyuan officer Zhang Guang killed his wife and bought release from prison with wealth; cases before and after could not decide it; Jinglue verified the facts and argued for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang of Wuyuan murdered his wife and bought off justice; Jinglue verified the facts and demanded execution.

sentences.zh: 既而有若女厲者進謝廷中，如光妻雲。

translations.literal: Afterward there seemed to be a furious woman who entered the court to thank him, like Guang's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Then a furious spirit like Guang's wife entered court to thank him.

sentences.zh: 遷大理司直。

translations.literal: He was moved to direct judge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He became direct judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 懷光屯咸陽，將襲東渭橋，召幕府計議。

translations.literal: Huai'guang camped at Xianyang and was about to strike the eastern Wei Bridge; he summoned the staff to plan.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang at Xianyang meant to strike the eastern Wei Bridge and called his staff.

sentences.zh: 景略曰：「殺朱泚，還軍諸道，杖策詣行在，此轉禍為福也。」

translations.literal: Jinglue said, "Kill Zhu Ci, return the army to the commands, take staff in hand and go to the temporary capital — this turns calamity into fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglue said, "Kill Zhu Ci, march the army home, and go to the emperor — that turns disaster to blessing.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 既出軍門，慟哭曰：「豈意此軍乃陷不義乎！」

translations.literal: Having left the army gate he wailed, "Did I think this army would fall into unrighteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Outside the gate he wailed that the army had turned unrighteous.

sentences.zh: 遂遁歸。

translations.literal: He then fled home.
translations.idiomatic: He fled home.

sentences.zh: 靈武節度使杜希全表置於府，累轉侍御史、豐州刺史。

translations.literal: The Lingwu military governor Du Xiquan memorialized to place him in the headquarters; he was repeatedly promoted to attendant censor and governor of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiquan of Lingwu took him on staff; he rose to attendant censor and governor of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 豐州當回紇通道，前刺史軟柔，每虜使至，與抗禮。

translations.literal: Fengzhou lay on the Uighur route; former governors were soft; whenever barbarian envoys came they met them as equals.
translations.idiomatic: Fengzhou lay on the Uighur road; soft governors had met envoys as equals.

sentences.zh: 時梅錄將軍入朝，景略欲折之，因郊勞，前遣人謂曰：「可汗新沒，欲吊使者。」

translations.literal: When General Meilu came to court Jinglue wished to humble him; at the suburban comfort feast he sent men ahead saying, "The qaghan has newly died — we wish to condole the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When Meilu came to court Jinglue meant to humble him; at the comfort feast he sent word that the qaghan had died and they would mourn.

sentences.zh: 乃坐高壟待之。

translations.literal: He then sat on a high mound to await him.
translations.idiomatic: He sat on a high mound to wait.

sentences.zh: 梅錄俯僂前哭，景略即撫之曰：「可汗棄代，助爾號慕。」

translations.literal: Meilu bowed forward and wept; Jinglue at once comforted him, saying, "The qaghan has left the world — I help you in your grief.
translations.idiomatic: Meilu bowed and wept; Jinglue comforted him for the qaghan's death.

sentences.zh: 於是虜容氣沮索，不敢抗，以父行呼景略。

translations.literal: Thereupon the barbarians' bearing was dejected and drawn in and they did not dare resist; they addressed Jinglue as father.
translations.idiomatic: The Uighurs slumped and dared not stand tall; they called him father.

sentences.zh: 自此回紇使至者，皆拜於廷，威名顯聞。

translations.literal: From this onward whenever Uighur envoys came they bowed in the court and his renown shone.
translations.idiomatic: After that Uighur envoys bowed in his hall and his fame spread.

sentences.zh: 希全忌之，誣奏，貶袁州司馬。

translations.literal: Xiquan envied him and memorialized falsely; he was demoted to army marshal of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiquan envied him, slandered him, and he was demoted to Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 希全死，遷左羽林將軍，對德宗延英殿，論奏衎衎，有大臣風。

translations.literal: When Xiquan died he was moved to general of the Left Feathered Forest; at audience in the Yanying Hall his discourse was expansive, with the air of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiquan died he entered the Left Feathered Forest; at Yanying Hall he spoke like a great minister.

sentences.zh: 會河東節度使李說病，以景略為太原少尹、行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When the Hedong military governor Li Yue fell ill Jinglue was made Taiyuan vice prefect and campaigning staff marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yue of Hedong fell ill; Jinglue became Taiyuan vice prefect and staff marshal.

sentences.zh: 時方鎮既重，故少召還者，惟不幸則司馬代之。

translations.literal: At that time the regional commands were already weighty; therefore few vice prefects were recalled — only if misfortune came did the staff marshal replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Commands were mighty; vice prefects rarely returned — only death brought the marshal up.

sentences.zh: 自說有疾，人心固屬景略矣。

translations.literal: From the time Yue fell ill men's hearts already belonged to Jinglue.
translations.idiomatic: From Yue's illness the army already looked to Jinglue.

sentences.zh: 會梅錄復入朝，說大會，虜人爭坐，說不敢遏，景略叱之，梅錄識其聲，驚拜曰：「非李豐州邪？」

translations.literal: When Meilu again entered court Yue held a great feast; the barbarians fought for seats; Yue did not dare restrain them; Jinglue shouted at them; Meilu recognized his voice, started in fear, and bowed, saying, "Are you not the Lord of Fengzhou?
translations.idiomatic: Meilu came again; at Yue's feast the tribes fought for seats; Jinglue shouted them down; Meilu knew his voice and cried, "Lord of Fengzhou!

sentences.zh: 遂就坐。

translations.literal: He then took his seat.
translations.idiomatic: He then sat.

sentences.zh: 將吏相顧嚴憚，說愈不平，賂中尉竇文場謀毀去之。

translations.literal: Officers looked at one another in stern awe; Yue was ever more resentful and bribed the palace commander Dou Wenchang to plot his removal.
translations.idiomatic: Officers stared in awe; Yue bribed Dou Wenchang to ruin him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，塞下傳言回紇將南寇，文場方侍帝傍，即言豐州當得良將，且舉景略，乃拜豐州刺史、天德軍西受降城都防禦使。

translations.literal: After more than a year rumor spread on the frontier that the Uighurs would raid south; Wenchang was attending the emperor and at once said Fengzhou needed a good general and recommended Jinglue; he was made governor of Fengzhou and defender of the western Shouxiang city of the Tiande army.
translations.idiomatic: A year later rumor said the Uighurs would strike south; Wenchang at court named Jinglue governor of Fengzhou and defender of Shouxiang.

sentences.zh: 窮塞苦寒，地塉鹵，邊戶勞悴。

translations.literal: The poor frontier was bitter cold, the soil salty and barren, and the border households worn out.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier was cold, the soil salt-poisoned, the people exhausted.

sentences.zh: 景略至，節用約己，與士同甘蓼，鑿咸應、永清二渠，溉田數百頃，儲稟器械畢具，威令肅然，聲雄北疆，回紇畏之。

translations.literal: When Jinglue arrived he husbanded expenses and restrained himself, shared hardship with the men, dug the Xianying and Yongqing canals, irrigated several hundred qing of fields, and stores and weapons were complete; discipline was stern and his name thundered on the northern border; the Uighurs feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He husbanded stores, shared hardship, dug canals, irrigated hundreds of qing, filled arsenals, and terrified the Uighurs.

sentences.zh: 卒於屯，年五十五。

translations.literal: He died in garrison at fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in camp at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 天下惜用景略才有所未盡。

translations.literal: The realm grieved that Jinglue's talent had not been fully used.
translations.idiomatic: The empire mourned that his talent was cut short.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 任迪簡，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Ren Dijian, a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Dijian came from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 天德李景略表佐其軍，嘗宴客，而行酒者誤進醢，景略用法嚴，迪簡不忍其死，飲為釂，徐以它辭請易之，歸衉血，不以聞，軍中悅其長者。

translations.literal: Li Jinglue of Tiande listed him on staff; at a feast the cup-bearer mistakenly served pickled meat; Jinglue's law was strict; Dijian could not bear that he die and drank the cup in his place, then slowly asked to exchange it with another excuse, returned vomiting blood, and did not report it; the army admired him as an elder of worth.
translations.idiomatic: On Jinglue's staff a cup-bearer served pickle by mistake; Jinglue's law was harsh; Dijian drank the cup for him, swapped it by ruse, vomited blood in secret, and the army loved him.

sentences.zh: 景略卒，舉軍請為帥，監軍使拘迪簡，不聽，眾大呼，破戶出之。

translations.literal: When Jinglue died the whole army asked that Dijian be commander; the army supervisor detained Dijian and would not agree; the crowd shouted loudly and broke the door to release him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglue died; the army wanted Dijian; the supervisor refused; they broke the door and freed him.

sentences.zh: 德宗遣使者察變，具得所以然，乃授豐州刺史、天德軍使。

translations.literal: Dezong sent an envoy to examine the disturbance and fully learned the reason; he was made governor of Fengzhou and commander of the Tiande army.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong investigated and made him governor of Fengzhou and Tiande commander.

sentences.zh: 由殿中侍御史授兼大夫、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: From attendant censor he was given the concurrent posts of Grand Master of the Palace and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: From attendant censor he became Grand Master of the Palace and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 入為太常少卿、太子左庶子。

translations.literal: He entered as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Director of Sacrifices and Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 張茂昭以易定歸，擢迪簡行軍司馬代之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Maozhao submitted Yiding, Dijian was advanced to campaigning staff marshal in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When Maozhao surrendered Yiding, Dijian replaced him as staff marshal.

sentences.zh: 大將楊伯玉據牙不納，眾殺之；

translations.literal: The great general Yang Boyu held headquarters and would not receive him; the crowd killed Boyu;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Boyu held headquarters and refused him; the troops killed Boyu;

sentences.zh: 別將張佐元復叛，迪簡斬以徇，乃入，以檢校工部尚書為節度使。

translations.literal: another general Zhang Zuoyuan rebelled again; Dijian executed him as a warning and then entered; he was made acting Minister of Works and military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuoyuan rebelled; Dijian beheaded him and entered as acting Minister of Works and governor.

sentences.zh: 承茂昭奢縱後，公私屈覂，欲饗士，無所給，至與下同糲食，身居戟戶。

translations.literal: Following Maozhao's luxury and license, public and private were strained; wishing to feast the troops he had nothing to give and shared coarse grain with the men, dwelling in a halberd gate.
translations.idiomatic: After Maozhao's excesses he had nothing to feast the troops with and ate coarse grain in a halberd gate with them.

sentences.zh: 逾月，軍中感其公，請安臥內，迪簡乃許。

translations.literal: After more than a month the army was moved by his fairness and asked him to rest within; Dijian then consented.
translations.idiomatic: A month later the army pitied him and begged him to sleep indoors; he agreed.

sentences.zh: 三年，上下完充。

translations.literal: In three years upper and lower were complete.
translations.idiomatic: In three years the command was whole.

sentences.zh: 以疾入，除工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered with illness and was made Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he entered as Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 不能朝，改太子賓客。

translations.literal: Unable to attend court he was changed to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to attend court he became Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈刑部尚書，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Minister of Justice and given the posthumous title Assisting.
translations.idiomatic: He died, was posthumously Minister of Justice, and titled Assisting.

sentences.zh: 張萬福，魏州元城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wanfu, a man of Yuancheng in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wanfu came from Yuancheng in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 三世明經，止縣令、州佐。

translations.literal: For three generations they passed the classics examination and stopped at county magistrate and prefectural aide.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations passed the classics exam and rose only to county magistrate or prefectural aide.

sentences.zh: 萬福以儒業不顯，乃學騎射，從王斛斯以別校征遼東，有功。

translations.literal: Wanfu did not shine in Confucian pursuit and therefore studied mounted archery; he followed Wang Husi as a separate commander in the Liaodong campaign and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Failing at Confucian office he took to archery, followed Wang Husi to Liaodong, and won merit.

sentences.zh: 李亙伐劉展，署為部將，效首萬級。

translations.literal: When Li Gen attacked Liu Zhan he was appointed a division commander and presented ten thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gen against Liu Zhan made him division commander; he sent up ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 累攝壽州刺史、舒廬壽都團練使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly acting governor of Shouzhou and commander of the Shu-Lu-Shou training circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly acting governor of Shouzhou and Shu-Lu-Shou commander.

sentences.zh: 州送租賦詣都，至潁，為盜所奪。

translations.literal: The prefecture sent rent to the capital; at Ying it was seized by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Rent bound for the capital was seized at Ying by bandits.

sentences.zh: 萬福領輕兵尾襲，賊倉卒不得戰，悉禽之，盡得所亡，並先掠人妻女、財畜萬計，還其家，不能自致者，給船車以遣。

translations.literal: Wanfu led light troops in pursuit; the bandits could not fight in haste and were all captured; all that was lost was recovered, together with wives, daughters, livestock, and wealth seized earlier by the tens of thousands; he returned them to their families; those who could not go home were given boats and carts to send them.
translations.idiomatic: Wanfu pursued with light troops, took every bandit, restored all stolen goods and families, and sent the stranded home by boat and cart.

sentences.zh: 真拜刺史，兼淮南節度副使。

translations.literal: He was formally made governor and also deputy military governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor and Huainan deputy military governor.

sentences.zh: 而節度崔圓忌之，失刺史，改鴻臚卿，使將千人鎮壽州，不以為恨。

translations.literal: The military governor Cui Yuan envied him; he lost the governorship and was changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, commanding a thousand men to garrison Shouzhou, without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan envied him; he lost Shouzhou, became Vice Director of Entertainments, garrisoned a thousand at Shouzhou, and did not complain.

sentences.zh: 時許杲以平盧行軍司馬將卒三千駐濠州，陰窺淮南。

translations.literal: At that time Xu Gao with three thousand men of the Pinglu campaigning army garrisoned Haozhou and secretly watched Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gao with three thousand Pinglu men garrisoned Haozhou and eyed Huainan.

sentences.zh: 圓使萬福攝濠州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuan had Wanfu act as governor of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan made Wanfu acting governor of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 杲聞，即移戍當塗。

translations.literal: When Gao heard of it he at once moved his garrison to Dangtu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao heard and moved to Dangtu.

sentences.zh: 賊陳莊陷舒州，圓又令攝舒州刺史，督淮南盜賊，窮破株黨。

translations.literal: The bandit Chen Zhuang took Shuzhou; Yuan again ordered him to act as governor of Shuzhou and supervise Huainan bandits, rooting out the cliques utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhuang took Shuzhou; Yuan sent Wanfu as acting governor to crush Huainan banditry.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年，召見。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali he was summoned to audience.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 3 he was summoned.

sentences.zh: 代宗曰：「欲一識卿面，且將以許杲累卿。」

translations.literal: Daizong said, "I wished to know your face once, and also to burden you with Xu Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong said, "I wished to see your face and to set you on Xu Gao.

sentences.zh: 萬福辭謝，因前曰：「陛下以一許杲召臣，如河北諸將叛，欲屬何人？」

translations.literal: Wanfu declined thanks and stepped forward, saying, "Your Majesty summons me for one Xu Gao — if the Hebei generals rebel, to whom will you entrust it?"
translations.idiomatic: Wanfu stepped forward: "You call me for Gao — if Hebei rebels, whom will you send?"

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「始為我了杲事，且當大用。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "First settle Gao's affair for me — then you will be greatly used."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed: "Settle Gao first — then we will use you greatly."

sentences.zh: 乃拜和州刺史兼行營防禦使，督盜淮南。

translations.literal: He was made governor of Hezhou and also campaigning defense commissioner, supervising Huainan bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Hezhou and campaigning commissioner over Huainan bandits.

sentences.zh: 萬福至州，杲懼，徙屯上元，過楚州，大掠，節度使韋元甫使萬福追討。

translations.literal: When Wanfu reached the prefecture Gao was afraid and moved his camp to Shangyuan; passing Chuzhou he plundered greatly; the military governor Wei Yuanfu sent Wanfu in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: At Hezhou Gao fled to Shangyuan, plundered Chuzhou; Wanfu was sent in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 未至，杲為其將康自勸所逐，自勸循淮鈔而東，萬福倍道追殺之，免者十三，盡還所剽於民。

translations.literal: Before he arrived Gao was driven off by his officer Kang Ziqin; Ziqin raided along the Huai eastward; Wanfu marched double time, pursued and killed him; only thirteen escaped; all plunder was returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came Gao was expelled by Kang Ziqin; Wanfu double-timed, killed Ziqin, spared thirteen, and returned all loot.

sentences.zh: 元甫將厚賞士，萬福曰：「官健坐仰衣食，無所事，今一小煩之，不足過賞，請用三之一。」

translations.literal: Yuanfu wished to reward the troops heavily; Wanfu said, "Soldiers sit and eat — for this small trouble it is not fit to over-reward; please use one third."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu wished to reward heavily; Wanfu said soldiers were paid to fight — one third was enough.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔褒美，賜具衣、宮錦十雙。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict of praise and bestowed full robes and ten pairs of palace brocade.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and gave robes and brocade.

sentences.zh: 久之，詔以本鎮兵千五百人防秋京西。

translations.literal: After a long while an edict ordered fifteen hundred troops of his command to guard the western capital in autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Later fifteen hundred of his troops were ordered to guard the western capital in autumn.

sentences.zh: 萬福詣揚州還所領兵。

translations.literal: Wanfu went to Yangzhou to return the troops he led.
translations.idiomatic: Wanfu went to Yangzhou to hand back his troops.

sentences.zh: 會元甫死，諸將願得萬福為帥，監軍使邀請之，對曰：「我非幸人，勿以此待我。」

translations.literal: When Yuanfu died the generals wished Wanfu as commander; the army supervisor invited him; he answered, "I am not a man of fortune — do not treat me so."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu died; generals wanted Wanfu; he refused: "I am no favorite of fate.

sentences.zh: 遂去。

translations.literal: He then left.
translations.idiomatic: He left.

sentences.zh: 以利州刺史鎮咸陽，且留宿衛。

translations.literal: He was made governor of Lizhou to garrison Xianyang and also remained on palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Lizhou at Xianyang and kept palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 李正己反，屯兵埇橋，江淮漕船積千餘不敢逾渦口。

translations.literal: When Li Zhengyi rebelled he massed troops at Yongqiao; more than a thousand Huai River grain barges piled up and dared not pass Wokou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengyi rebelled at Yongqiao; a thousand grain barges dared not pass Wokou.

sentences.zh: 德宗乃以萬福為濠州刺史，召謂曰：「先帝改爾名正者，所以褒也。

translations.literal: Dezong then made Wanfu governor of Haozhou and summoned him, saying, "The former emperor changed your name to Zheng to praise you.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong made him governor of Haozhou and said, "Your former name Zheng was praise.

sentences.zh: 朕謂江淮草木亦知爾威名，若從所改，恐賊不曉是卿也。」

translations.literal: I think even the grass and trees of Jiang-Huai know your dread name — if we follow the change perhaps the rebels will not know it is you.
translations.idiomatic: Even Jiang-Huai's grass knows your name — keep the old name lest rebels not know you.

sentences.zh: 復賜舊名。

translations.literal: His former name was restored.
translations.idiomatic: His old name was restored.

sentences.zh: 萬福因馳至渦口，駐馬於岸，悉發漕船相銜進，賊兵倚岸熟視不敢動。

translations.literal: Wanfu galloped to Wokou, halted his horse on the bank, and sent all the grain barges forward linked one after another; the rebel soldiers leaned on the bank and watched closely and did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: Wanfu raced to Wokou, drove every barge through while rebels on the bank watched and did not stir.

sentences.zh: 改泗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was changed to governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 魏州饑，父子相賣，萬福曰：「魏州吾鄉里，安忍其困？」

translations.literal: Weizhou had famine; fathers and sons sold one another; Wanfu said, "Weizhou is my home — how can I bear its distress?
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou starved; men sold kin; Wanfu said, "Weizhou is my home — I cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 令兄子將米百車餉之，贖魏人自賣者，給資遣之。

translations.literal: He ordered his brother's son to take a hundred carts of grain to relieve it, ransomed those of Weizhou who had sold themselves, and gave traveling funds to send them off.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a hundred carts of grain, ransomed the sold, and gave them passage money.

sentences.zh: 為杜亞所忌，召拜右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Du Ya envied him and summoned him as Grand General of the Right Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya envied him and called him Grand General of the Right Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 及見，帝驚曰：「亞乃言爾昏耄，何邪？」

translations.literal: On audience the emperor started and said, "Ya said you were senile — what of it?
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor cried, "Ya called you senile — how?

sentences.zh: 詔圖形淩煙閣，數賜與，並敕度支籍口畜給其費。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his likeness painted in the Lingyan Pavilion; he was repeatedly bestowed gifts, and the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to register his household for stipend.
translations.idiomatic: His portrait was ordered for Lingyan Pavilion, gifts poured forth, and the Ministry registered his stipend.

sentences.zh: 陽城等詣延英門論裴延齡事，伏閣不去，帝震怒，左右懼不測。

translations.literal: Yang Cheng and others went to the Yanying Gate to argue the affair of Pei Yanling and lay before the gate without leaving; the emperor was greatly angered and those beside him feared the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cheng and others argued Pei Yanling at Yanying Gate and would not leave; the emperor raged and courtiers feared blood.

sentences.zh: 萬福大言曰：「國有直臣，天下無慮矣。

translations.literal: Wanfu cried aloud, "The state has upright ministers — the realm has no worry.
translations.idiomatic: Wanfu shouted, "The state has upright ministers — the realm is safe.

sentences.zh: 吾年八十，與見盛事。」

translations.literal: I am eighty and have seen a grand affair.
translations.idiomatic: I am eighty and have seen glory.

sentences.zh: 遍揖城等勞之，天下益重其名。

translations.literal: He bowed to Cheng and the others everywhere and comforted them; the realm esteemed his name the more.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed to Cheng and comforted them; the world honored him more.

sentences.zh: 以工部尚書致仕，卒，年九十。

translations.literal: He retired as Minister of Works and died at ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Minister of Works and died at ninety.

sentences.zh: 萬福自始終祿食七十年，未嘗一日言病。

translations.literal: From first to last Wanfu drew salary seventy years and never spoke of illness one day.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy years on salary he never once claimed illness.

sentences.zh: 蒞凡九州，皆有惠愛。

translations.literal: Wherever he governed among the nine provinces there was kind favor.
translations.idiomatic: In nine provinces he governed there was kindness.

sentences.zh: 初，在泗州，遇李希烈反，陳少遊悉以部刺史妻子質揚州，萬福獨不遣。

translations.literal: At first in Sizhou, when Li Xilie rebelled, Chen Shaoyou sent all the prefectural governors' wives and children as hostages to Yangzhou; Wanfu alone would not send them.
translations.idiomatic: At Sizhou when Xilie rebelled Shaoyou took governors' families hostage at Yangzhou; Wanfu alone refused.

sentences.zh: 謂使者：「為我白公，妻老且鬼，不足慁公意。」

translations.literal: He told the envoy, "Tell my lord for me: my wife is old and already a ghost — not worth troubling my lord's mind.
translations.idiomatic: He told the envoy, "Tell your master my wife is old as death — no need to trouble him.

sentences.zh: 卒不行，人稱其直。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go; men praised his uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: He never sent them; men praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 高固高固，不知何許人，或言四世祖侃，永徽中為北庭安撫使，禽車鼻可汗，以功為安東都護。

translations.literal: Gao Gu. Gao Gu — it is not known where he was from; some say his fourth-generation ancestor Kan in the Yonghui era was northern pacifier, captured the Chebi qaghan, and by merit was made protector of the east.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gu — birthplace unknown; some say his fourth-generation ancestor Kan in Yonghui was northern pacifier, took the Chebi qaghan, and became Anton protector.

sentences.zh: 固生微賤，為家所賣，轉為渾瑊童奴，字黃芩。

translations.literal: Gu was born in humble station, was sold by his family, and became the boy slave Hun Zhan, styled Huangqin.
translations.idiomatic: Born low, sold by kin, he became Hun Zhan's slave boy Huangqin.

sentences.zh: 性敏惠，有旅力，善騎射，能讀《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: He was clever and quick, had traveling strength, was skilled in mounted archery, and could read Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Clever, strong, skilled in archery, he read Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 瑊愛養之，以齊有高固，因以名，以乳媼女女固。

translations.literal: Zhan loved and raised him; because Qi had a Gao Gu he therefore gave the name, and gave him the wet nurse's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan raised him; because Qi had a Gao Gu he gave the name and married him to his nurse's daughter.

sentences.zh: 從瑊屯朔方。

translations.literal: He followed Zhan to garrison Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhan to Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 德宗在奉天，固仍從瑊，賊突入東壅門，固引銳士長刀殺賊數十人，曳車塞闔，賊不能入。

translations.literal: When Dezong was at Fengtian Gu still followed Zhan; rebels burst into the eastern Yong gate; Gu led sharp troops with long blades and killed several tens of rebels, dragged carts to block the gate, and the rebels could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengtian rebels broke the eastern Yong gate; Gu led blade men, killed dozens, blocked the gate with carts.

sentences.zh: 封渤海郡王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Prince of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 李懷光反，使邠寧留後張昕將兵萬人先趣河中，固在行，乃伺間入帳下，斬昕首以徇，拜檢校右散騎常侍、前軍兵馬使。

translations.literal: When Li Huai'guang rebelled he sent the Binning rear commander Zhang Xin with ten thousand men first to hurry to Hezhong; Gu was on the march; he watched for an opening, entered the tent, beheaded Xin to show the army, and was made acting Right Regular Attendant and vanguard horse commander.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang sent Zhang Xin with ten thousand to Hezhong; Gu on the march entered the tent, beheaded Xin, and was made acting Right Attendant and vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 貞元十七年，邠寧節度使楊朝晟卒，詔將並邠寧、朔方為一軍，議以李朝寀為節度，劉南金副之，以詢邠軍，咸曰：「如詔。」

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan the Binning military governor Yang Chaocheng died; an edict was to merge Binning and Shuofang into one army; it was discussed to make Li Chaoqin military governor and Liu Nanjin deputy; when Binning was consulted all said, "As the edict says."
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 17 Yang Chaocheng died; Binning and Shuofang were to merge; Li Chaoqin was to command with Liu Nanjin deputy; Binning agreed.

sentences.zh: 數日復劫固為帥，固曰：「然能聽吾言。

translations.literal: Several days later they again compelled Gu as commander; Gu said, "Yet you must heed my words.
translations.idiomatic: Days later they forced Gu as commander; Gu said, "Hear me first.

sentences.zh: 乃可。」

translations.literal: Then it may be.
translations.idiomatic: Then perhaps.

sentences.zh: 眾唯唯。

translations.literal: The crowd assented.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd agreed.

sentences.zh: 固徇曰：「毋殺人，毋肆掠！」

translations.literal: Gu proclaimed, "Do not kill, do not plunder wildly!
translations.idiomatic: Gu proclaimed, "No killing, no looting!

sentences.zh: 三軍皆順悅。

translations.literal: The three armies all submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies obeyed gladly.

sentences.zh: 帝亦念固功，乃拜邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor also remembered Gu's merit and made him military governor of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remembered his merit and made him governor of Binning.

sentences.zh: 固本宿將，且寬厚，人皆安之。

translations.literal: Gu was originally a veteran commander and moreover generous; all were reassured.
translations.idiomatic: A veteran and generous, he reassured all.

sentences.zh: 然久在散位，數為儕類輕笑。

translations.literal: Yet he had long been in loose posts and was several times lightly laughed at by his peers.
translations.idiomatic: Long in minor posts he had been mocked by peers.

sentences.zh: 及受命，眾多懼，固一釋不問。

translations.literal: When he received the appointment many were afraid; Gu released it all without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Many feared on his appointment; Gu forgave all.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，檢校尚書右僕射，入為右羽林統軍。

translations.literal: In Xianzong's time he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and entered as commander of the Right Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianzong he became acting Right Vice Director and commander of the Right Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈陜州大都督。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Governor of Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Grand Governor of Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 郝比，不記其鄉里。

translations.literal: Hao Bi — his district is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Bi — homeland unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 貞元中為臨涇鎮將，嘗從數百騎出野，還，說節度使馬璘曰：「臨涇扼洛口，其川饒衍，利畜牧。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan he was commander of Linjing Fort; he once went out to the wilds with several hundred horse and returned, telling the military governor Ma Lin, "Linjing holds the Luokou; its rivers are rich and broad, good for pasture.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan he commanded Linjing; returning from a ride of hundreds he told Ma Lin, "Linjing holds Luokou — rich pasture.

sentences.zh: 其西走戎道，曠數百里皆流沙，無水草。

translations.literal: Westward the road to the barbarians runs hundreds of li through desert without grass or water.
translations.idiomatic: Westward lies desert hundreds of li without grass or water.

sentences.zh: 願城之，為休養便地。」

translations.literal: I wish to wall it as a place of rest and supply.
translations.idiomatic: Wall it for rest and supply.

sentences.zh: 比出，或謂璘曰：「比言信然。

translations.literal: When Bi had gone out someone said to Lin, "Bi's words are indeed true.
translations.idiomatic: After Bi left someone told Lin, "Bi is right.

sentences.zh: 雖然，公所以蒙恩大幸，以邊防未固也。

translations.literal: Even so, the great favor you enjoy from grace is because the frontier is not yet secure.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your grace is great because the frontier is not secure.

sentences.zh: 上心日夜念此，故厚於公。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart day and night thinks of this; therefore he is generous to you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thinks of this daily; hence your bounty.

sentences.zh: 今若用比言，則邊已安，尚何事為？」

translations.literal: If Bi's words are now used the frontier will be secure — what then remains to be done?
translations.idiomatic: If Bi's plan is adopted the frontier will be secure — what task will remain for you?

sentences.zh: 璘遂不聽。

translations.literal: Lin therefore did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Lin would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 及段佑代節度，比又說曰：「天寶時，天下以兵為防，獨西戎耳。

translations.literal: When Duan You replaced him as military governor Bi again said, "In Tianbao times the realm took soldiers as defense — only the western barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan You succeeded him as military governor, Bi spoke again: "In the Tianbao era the empire garrisoned only the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 而塞至京師且萬里。

translations.literal: Yet the frontier to the capital was ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the passes lay ten thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 自祿山反，西陲盡亡，寰內為邊郡。

translations.literal: From the time Lushan rebelled the western frontier was wholly lost and the heartland became border commands.
translations.idiomatic: After Lushan rebelled the west was lost and the interior itself became a frontier.

sentences.zh: 每虜入寇，驅井閭父子與馬牛，焚積聚，殘室廬，邊人耗盡。

translations.literal: Whenever the barbarians entered to raid they drove household fathers and sons with horses and cattle, burned stores, ruined houses — border people were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Each raid drove out peasants and cattle, burned granaries, wrecked homes, until the border was emptied.

sentences.zh: 今若築臨涇以折虜勢，便甚。」

translations.literal: Now if Linjing is walled to break the barbarians' momentum it would be very advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Wall Linjing now and you will break their momentum.

sentences.zh: 佑唯許，請於朝。

translations.literal: You only assented and requested it of the court.
translations.idiomatic: You assented alone and memorialized the court.

sentences.zh: 卒詔城臨涇，為行原州，以比為刺史，戍之。

translations.literal: At last an edict walled Linjing as Xingyuan Prefecture, made Bi its governor, and garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: At last an edict walled Linjing as Xingyuan Prefecture, made Bi its governor, and stationed him there.

sentences.zh: 自是虜不敢過臨涇。

translations.literal: From this the barbarians did not dare pass Linjing.
translations.idiomatic: After that the barbarians did not dare cross Linjing.

sentences.zh: 玭在邊積三十年，每討賊，不持糗糧，取之於敵。

translations.literal: Bi was on the frontier thirty years in all; whenever he attacked rebels he did not carry dry rations but took from the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Bi served on the frontier thirty years; on campaign he carried no dry rations but lived off the enemy.

sentences.zh: 獲虜必刳剔而歸其屍，虜大畏，道其名以怖啼兒。

translations.literal: Whenever he captured barbarians he flayed them and returned the corpses; the barbarians greatly feared him and spoke his name to frighten crying children.
translations.idiomatic: Captives he flayed and sent back; the tribes feared him so deeply that mothers frightened crying children with his name.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校左散騎常侍、涇原行營節度使，封保定郡王。

translations.literal: He was moved to acting Left Regular Attendant and Jingyuan campaigning military governor and enfeoffed Prince of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Left Regular Attendant and Jingyuan campaigning military governor, and enfeoffed Prince of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 贊普常等故身鑄金象，令於國曰：「得生比者，以金比償之。」

translations.literal: The Tibetan king Trisong Detsen and others cast a gold image of his living body and ordered in the state, "Whoever captures Bi alive will be paid gold equal to Bi.
translations.idiomatic: King Trisong Detsen and others cast a gold statue of him in life and proclaimed throughout the realm that whoever took him alive would be paid its weight in gold.

sentences.zh: 朝廷畏失名將，徙為慶州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: The court feared losing a famed general and moved him to governor of Qingzhou; he died.
translations.idiomatic: The court, fearing to lose a famous commander, transferred him to Qingzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 佑，本郭子儀牙將，從征伐有功。

translations.literal: You was originally Guo Ziyi's guard officer and had merit in campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Duan You had been a guard officer under Guo Ziyi and won merit on campaign.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，為涇原節度使，虜畏憚之。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan he was military governor of Jingyuan and the barbarians feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenyuan he was military governor of Jingyuan, and the barbarians stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 終右神策大將軍。

translations.literal: He ended as Grand General of the Right Divine Strategy Army.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Grand General of the Right Divine Strategy Army.

sentences.zh: 史敬奉者，靈州人。

translations.literal: Shi Jingfeng was a man of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingfeng came from Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 事朔方軍為牙將。

translations.literal: He served the Shuofang army as a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Shuofang army as a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 元和中，吐蕃數犯塞，十四年，敬奉白節度使杜叔良，請兵三千，賫一月糧，深入虜地，分賊勢。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era Tibet repeatedly raided the passes; in the fourteenth year Jingfeng told the military governor Du Shuliang, asking for three thousand men and one month's grain to penetrate deep into barbarian land and divide the enemy's force.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe, as Tibet raided again and again, Jingfeng in the fourteenth year asked Du Shuliang for three thousand men and a month's rations to strike deep and split the enemy.

sentences.zh: 叔良以二千兵予之，行十餘日，不聞問，皆謂已歿。

translations.literal: Shuliang gave him two thousand; after more than ten days on the road there was no word and all said he was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Shuliang gave him two thousand; ten days passed without news and men assumed he was lost.

sentences.zh: 敬奉乃由間道繞出虜後，部落奔駭，因大破之，驅其餘眾於瓠蘆河，獲馬牛雜畜迨萬數。

translations.literal: Jingfeng by a hidden road circled behind the barbarians; the tribes fled in alarm; he therefore broke them utterly, drove the remainder to the Hulu River, and captured horses, cattle, and mixed livestock nearly ten thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfeng took a hidden track behind the tribes; they fled in panic; he routed them utterly, drove the remnant to the Hulu River, and seized nearly ten thousand head of horse and cattle.

sentences.zh: 賜實封五十戶。

translations.literal: He was granted a substantive fief of fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a substantive fief of fifty households.

sentences.zh: 敬奉遳陋，類不勝衣，其走逐奔馬，挾鞍勒以上，而後羈帶之，矛矢在手，前無強敵。

translations.literal: Jingfeng was short and ugly, as if clothes would not hang on him; yet in chasing a running horse he would seize the saddle and girth and climb up, then afterward tighten the reins; with spear and arrow in hand none strong stood before him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfeng was small and mean in appearance, yet chasing a galloping horse he would seize saddle and girth, swing himself up, then tighten the reins; spear and bow in hand, no foe stood before him.

sentences.zh: 甥侄部曲二百人，每出輒分其隊為四五，隨水草，數日不相知，及相遇，已皆有獲。

translations.literal: Two hundred nephews and clan soldiers — whenever he went out he divided the detachments into four or five, following grass and water; several days without meeting, when they met each already had booty.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred nephews and clan troops — on each raid he split them into four or five bands by pasture; days might pass without contact, yet when they met each band already had spoil.

sentences.zh: 與鳳翔將野詩良輔及郝比皆以名雄邊。

translations.literal: With the Fengxiang general Ye Shi Liangfu and Hao Bi he was famed on the border by name.
translations.idiomatic: With Ye Shi Liangfu of Fengxiang and Hao Bi he shared a frontier fame.

sentences.zh: 良輔者，後為隴州刺史。

translations.literal: Liangfu later became governor of Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liangfu later became governor of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣使至吐蕃，虜輒言：「唐家稱和好豈妄邪！

translations.literal: When the court sent envoys to Tibet the barbarians always said, "Does the Tang speak of good peace in vain!
translations.idiomatic: When the court sent envoys to Tibet the tribes would say, "Does the House of Tang speak of peace for nothing!

sentences.zh: 不爾，安得任良輔為隴州刺史？」

translations.literal: Otherwise how could Ren Liangfu be made governor of Longzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: If not, how could Ren Liangfu be appointed governor of Longzhou?"
